definition_zh: 偶尔的；间或发生的；偶然的；临时凑用的；不定期的
definition_en: happening or appearing from time to time rather than regularly, arising by chance, and made or kept for only a particular occasion
core_image: 一扇老木门整年关着，门轴上的灰积了薄薄一层
scene: 旧书店的卷帘门一年只拉起几次，门口的招牌褪了色，附近的人倒都记得它。An occasional customer still pushes the door open on Saturday mornings.
sceneCN: 这里的 occasional 是「偶尔的」（第 1 个义项：隔一段时间才发生一次）；句意为偶尔仍有顾客在星期六上午推门进来。图中可辨识物件：卷帘门、褪色招牌、门轴上的灰。

pos.zh: 偶尔的；偶然的；临时的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 occasio（时机、机会）经古法语进入英语，义为「场合；时机」
由 occasional 加 -ly 构成，义为「偶尔地；间或」
由 occasional 加 -ness 构成，义为「偶发性；不经常的状态」

senses.title: Happening from time to time
senses.definition: happening or appearing now and then, with gaps of time in between, rather than in a steady pattern
senses.definitionCN: 时而发生或出现，中间隔着一段段时间，而不是稳定持续地进行
senses.example: She made occasional visits to the village where she grew up.
senses.exampleCN: 她偶尔回一趟自己长大的村子。
senses.why: The Latin stem occasio named a moment that befalls a person, so an occasional event is one that only lands on certain moments instead of staying.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 occasio 指落到某人头上的某个时刻，所以 occasional 的事情只是在某些时刻落到眼前，而不是一直停在那里。

senses.title: Arising by chance rather than by plan
senses.definition: coming about because of chance circumstances, not because someone arranged or intended it
senses.definitionCN: 因偶然情况而发生，而不是有人安排或有意为之
senses.example: An occasional meeting at the station led to a long friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 在车站的一次偶然相遇带来了一段长久的友谊。
senses.why: Since occasio could mean a lucky or unlucky turn of events, the adjective also describes what simply happens to us, without a plan behind it.
senses.whyCN: 既然 occasio 也可指运气好坏的一次转折，这个形容词便也能描述不由计划、只是落到我们头上的事。

senses.title: Kept or used only for a particular occasion
senses.titleCN: 临时的；应景的；备用凑用的
senses.definition: made, kept or used only now and then, for a special purpose, such as a chair set out when guests come
senses.definitionCN: 只为隔一段时间出现的特定用途而制作、保存或使用，例如来客时才摆出的椅子
senses.example: They kept an occasional table folded against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们家里有一张折叠着靠墙放的备用小桌。
senses.why: Furniture that comes out only on certain occasions took the adjective as a name, because the object leads the same intermittent life as the event.
senses.whyCN: 只在某些场合才搬出来的家具也用这个形容词命名，因为物件过着和「偶尔发生的事」同样断续的生活。

senses.title: Not regular in time or amount
senses.definition: not fixed to a schedule, so it cannot be counted on to appear at set intervals
senses.definitionCN: 没有固定排期，因此不能指望它按固定间隔出现
senses.example: The clinic offers occasional free checks for older residents.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为老年居民不定期提供免费检查。
senses.why: Once a thing happens only on some occasions, nothing about it can be regular, so the word also denies a timetable without denying that it happens at all.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既然只在某些时候发生，就谈不上规律，于是这个词否定的是时刻表，而不是它会发生。

intro.en: Occasional is an English adjective built on occasion, whose Latin stem names a moment that falls to someone; the whole family turns on the idea of something that arrives rather than continues.
intro.cn: occasional 是英语在 occasion 之上构成的形容词，其拉丁词干指「落到某人头上的时刻」；这一族词都围绕「降临而非持续」这个想法。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall, and it is the source of many English words about things that happen, befall or simply drop.
items.cn: cadere 意为落下，是英语中一大批表示「发生、降临、跌落」的词来源。

items.en: Ob- plus cadere gave occidere, to fall toward or upon something, used of the sun going down and of events coming to a person.
items.cn: ob- 与 cadere 合成 occidere，意为「朝某物落下、落到某物上」，既用于太阳西沉，也用于事件临到某人。

items.en: Occasio named the moment when something falls into place, hence an opportunity or an occasion; it was also the name of a Roman goddess of the opportune moment.
items.cn: occasio 指事情正好落定的那个时刻，因此是「机会、场合」；它也是罗马神话中「恰当时机」女神的名字。

items.en: Old French kept occasion as a word for a chance, a cause or a particular time, and English borrowed it in that bundle of senses.
items.cn: 古法语保留 occasion，指机会、缘由或特定的时刻，英语把这几个意思一并借了进来。

items.en: English added the adjective ending -al to occasion, so occasional first meant 'belonging to an occasion' and then 'happening only on some occasions'.
items.cn: 英语给 occasion 加上形容词后缀 -al，于是 occasional 先表示「属于某一场合的」，后来才表示「只在某些场合发生的」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for a falling moment; the near-meaning group collects words for things that happen rarely or unevenly.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「落下的时刻」这一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示稀少或断续发生的词。

entries.definition: A particular time when something happens, or a reason for doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的特定时刻，或做某事的缘由。

entries.definition: Now and then, at times that are not regular.
entries.definitionCN: 时而；不定时地。

entries.definition: A rhythm or flow, especially of sound or speech, from the Latin word for falling.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指声音或话语的节律，源自拉丁语中「落下」的词。

entries.definition: Something that happens by chance and is not planned.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然发生、并非计划中的事；事故。

entries.definition: Happening only here and there, in scattered and unpredictable moments.
entries.definitionCN: 零散发生、时地不可预测的。

entries.definition: Stopping and starting again at intervals rather than running continuously.
entries.definitionCN: 时断时续，而不是连续进行的。

entries.definition: Not happening often, so that long gaps lie between the times it does.
entries.definitionCN: 不常发生，发生的间隔很长。

entries.definition: Not following a fixed pattern or timetable.
entries.definitionCN: 不按固定规律或时刻表进行的。

normalIntro.en: The word is occasion wearing the adjective ending -al, so every hook comes back to the picture of a moment that only sometimes falls into place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 occasion 穿上形容词后缀 -al，所以每条记忆钩子都回到「只有某些时候才正好落定」的画面。

normal.en: Occasion is the noun behind the adjective, and -al simply means 'belonging to', so occasional belongs to certain occasions only.
normal.cn: occasion 是这个形容词背后的名词，-al 只表示「属于……的」，所以 occasional 只属于某些场合。

normal.en: Occasio in Latin was the moment something fell into place, which links the word to cadere, to fall.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 occasio 是事情正好落定的那一刻，这把它与 cadere（落下）连在一起。

normal.en: Occasionally is just occasional plus -ly, the plain adverb for now and then.
normal.cn: occasionally 只是 occasional 加 -ly，就是表示「时而」的普通副词。

normal.en: An occasional chair or table is an object kept for the times guests arrive, so furniture carries the same intermittent habit.
normal.cn: occasional chair 或 occasional table 是为来客时才用的物件，于是家具也带着同样「时有时无」的习性。

normal.en: In occasional showers, the adjective softens the forecast: rain will come, but not steadily.
normal.cn: 在 occasional showers 里，这个形容词软化了预报：雨会下，但不会连绵不断。

abstract.en: An occasional thing is defined less by what it is than by the size of the gaps around it.
abstract.cn: 偶尔发生的事，与其说由它本身定义，不如说由它周围的空隙大小定义。

abstract.en: Calling a moment an occasion admits that time is not a line but a series of landings.
abstract.cn: 把某一刻称作 occasion，就是承认时间不是一条直线，而是一连串的落点。

abstract.en: A word built on 'falling' reminds us that what happens to us often arrives rather than gets arranged.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在「落下」之上的词提醒人：落到我们头上的事，多半是降临，而不是安排。

examples.en: He still makes occasional trips to the coast to fish.
examples.cn: 他仍偶尔去海边钓鱼。

examples.en: Occasional heavy rain slowed the harvest but did not stop it.
examples.cn: 偶尔的大雨拖慢了收割，却没有让它停下来。

examples.en: The spare room has an occasional bed for guests.
examples.cn: 备用房间里有一张供客人临时使用的床。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶开身」——身子偶尔才开一次门，平时都关着；记住 occasional 是偶尔的。

root: 由 occasion 加形容词后缀 -al 构成；occasion 来自拉丁语 occasio（时机、机会），其词干 occidere 意为「落到某物上」，再上溯 cadere（落下）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a moment that only sometimes falls into place; from it come chance happenings, objects kept for such moments, and the plain denial of a regular schedule.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是只有某些时候才落定的一个时刻；由此分出偶然发生的事、为这种时刻留着的物件，以及「没有固定排期」这一层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old wooden door that stays shut all year, with a thin layer of dust on its hinge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇老木门整年关着，门轴上积着一层薄灰。

branches.en: a shop door raised on a few Saturday mornings
branches.cn: 几个星期六上午才拉起的店门

branches.en: two strangers meeting at a station by luck
branches.cn: 两个陌生人在车站碰巧相遇

branches.en: a folding table kept against the wall for guests
branches.cn: 靠墙收着、来客才用的折叠桌

branches.en: a clinic with no fixed day for free checks
branches.cn: 没有固定免费检查日的诊所

branches.en: the same irregular rhythm seen in events and in services
branches.cn: 事件与服务中同一种不规则的节奏

intro.en: The word is a Latin moment-noun plus an English adjective ending; behind the noun sit a prefix and a verb of falling.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁语「时刻」名词加一个英语形容词后缀构成；名词背后还有一个前缀和表示「落下」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cadere, occidere and occasio are all recorded, and they give the family its picture of something falling into place at a certain moment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere、occidere、occasio 都有记录，为这一族词提供了「某物在某一刻落定」的画面。

items.meaning: a moment that falls into place
a particular time or a reason

definition_zh: 偶尔；有时；间或
definition_en: sometimes, but not often, and without a regular pattern
core_image: 一本日历上零星画着几个小圈，多数日子空白
scene: 老式收音机会在深夜突然冒出杂音。The old radio occasionally crackles late at night.
sceneCN: 这里指不规律地偶尔发生（第 3 个义项：以不规则间隔出现）；句意为这台旧收音机深夜偶尔会噼啪作响；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 偶尔；有时；间或

derivatives.zh: 场合；时机
偶尔的；间或的
偶因论（哲学用语）

senses.title: Sometimes but not often
senses.definition: at times, with long gaps between occurrences
senses.definitionCN: 有时发生，但两次之间间隔较长
senses.example: I occasionally walk to work when the weather is fine.
senses.exampleCN: 天气好的时候，我偶尔步行去上班。
senses.why: The adverb sits on the lower part of the frequency scale, below sometimes and well below often.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词处在频率刻度的较低位置，低于「有时」，远低于「经常」。

senses.title: Sentence-opening frequency frame
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence, setting a sporadic pattern
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，为整句设定「零星发生」的模式
senses.example: Occasionally, the system fails without any warning.
senses.exampleCN: 偶尔，系统会在毫无预警的情况下失灵。
senses.why: The front position frames the whole event as an exception to the normal case.
senses.whyCN: 句首位置把整个事件框成正常情形之外的例外。

senses.title: At irregular intervals
senses.definition: happening without a fixed schedule or pattern
senses.definitionCN: 没有固定时间表或规律地发生
senses.example: The machine occasionally jams during heavy use.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器在高负荷使用时会偶尔卡住。
senses.why: The word denies regularity: the events happen, but no rhythm can be predicted.
senses.whyCN: 这个词否认规律性：事情会发生，却预测不出节奏。

senses.title: Now and then in speech
senses.definition: used in relaxed speech for an activity done from time to time
senses.definitionCN: 在轻松口语中指不时做一次的活动
senses.example: We occasionally meet for coffee after work.
senses.exampleCN: 我们下班后偶尔一起喝杯咖啡。
senses.why: The conversational register makes the word a soft way to describe a loose habit.
senses.whyCN: 口语语域让这个词成为描述松散习惯的柔和说法。

senses.title: Sporadic in technical writing
senses.definition: of faults or events that appear intermittently under certain conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指故障或事件在特定条件下间歇出现
senses.example: Errors occur occasionally when the load exceeds the limit.
senses.exampleCN: 当负载超过上限时，错误会偶尔出现。
senses.why: Technical reports use the word to admit a fault without claiming it is constant or reproducible.
senses.whyCN: 技术报告用它承认故障存在，却不声称它持续不断或可稳定复现。

senses.title: Deliberate understatement
senses.definition: used to make a frequent habit sound rarer than it is
senses.definitionCN: 用来把频繁的习惯说得比实际更稀少
senses.example: He occasionally drinks more than he should.
senses.exampleCN: 他偶尔会喝得超过应有的量。
senses.why: The choice of a low-frequency word can soften a description that the facts would support more strongly.
senses.whyCN: 选用低频率的词可以软化描述，而事实本可支持更强的说法。

senses.title: As an exception
senses.definition: used of a case that departs from the usual rule
senses.definitionCN: 用于偏离通常规则的情形
senses.example: Permission is occasionally granted for late applications.
senses.exampleCN: 逾期申请偶尔会获得许可。
senses.why: The word marks the exception that proves the rule, keeping the general statement intact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出「证明规则」的例外，从而保住一般性说法。

senses.title: In older formal prose
senses.definition: in literary or dated writing, a refined substitute for sometimes
senses.definitionCN: 在文学或旧式文字中，作为「有时」的雅致替代
senses.example: The lake is occasionally visited by migrating birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这片湖泊间或有候鸟造访。
senses.why: The formal written use sounds more measured than sometimes and often appears in descriptive prose.
senses.whyCN: 正式书面用法比「有时」更有分寸，常见于描写性散文。

intro.en: Occasionally comes from the Latin verb for falling down or happening, through its noun and English adjective, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「落下、发生」的动词，经名词与英语形容词，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The verb cadere means to fall, as in a falling event.
items.cn: 动词意为「落下」，如事件降临。

items.en: The prefix ob-, meaning towards or upon, plus cadere gives occidere, to fall upon or set.
items.cn: 表示「朝向、落在」的前缀与「落下」合成「落到……上、沉降」。

items.en: The noun occasio names a chance that falls at one's feet, hence an occasion or opportunity.
items.cn: 名词指落到脚边的机会，也就是时机、场合。

items.en: English occasion comes through French and gives the adjective occasional, meaning happening now and then.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入「场合」，并派生形容词，意为「偶尔发生的」。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern usage places the adverb below sometimes on the scale of frequency.
items.cn: 现代用法把它排在频率刻度上低于「有时」的位置。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin falling-root, including a look-alike from a different root; the second group orders expressions of frequency.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「落下」词根，其中包括一个形近但不同源的词；第二组按频率排列近义说法。

entries.definition: A particular time or event; the noun behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的时刻或事件；副词背后的名词。

entries.definition: Happening from time to time; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 不时发生的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: A philosophical view that events are caused directly by God on each occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 一种哲学观点，认为每次事件都由神直接引起。

entries.definition: Western; built on the Latin word for sunset, not on occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 西方的；由拉丁语「日落」构成，与「场合」无关。

entries.definition: On some occasions, more often than occasionally.
entries.definitionCN: 在某些场合，频率高于「偶尔」。

entries.definition: At intervals, without a fixed schedule.
entries.definitionCN: 间隔地，没有固定时间表。

entries.definition: A conversational phrase for an irregular low frequency.
entries.definitionCN: 口语短语，表示不规律的低频率。

entries.definition: In scattered, unpredictable instances.
entries.definitionCN: 以零散、不可预测的零星方式。

entries.definition: Stopping and starting again, often of a physical process.
entries.definitionCN: 断断续续地，多用于物理过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real falling-root and the real position of the word on the frequency scale.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「落下」词根，以及这个词在频率刻度上的真实位置。

normal.en: The root means to fall, so the event drops in now and then rather than on schedule.
normal.cn: 词根意为「落下」，所以事件是不定时掉进来，而不是按日程来。

normal.en: It sits below sometimes and far below often on the ladder of frequency.
normal.cn: 在频率阶梯上，它低于「有时」，远低于「经常」。

normal.en: Said first, it warns the listener that the next event is an exception.
normal.cn: 放在句首，它提醒听者接下来的事件只是例外。

normal.en: In a technical report it keeps a fault real without making it constant.
normal.cn: 在技术报告里，它让故障真实存在，却不把它说成持续不断。

normal.en: Used of a habit, it can politely make the habit sound rarer than it is.
normal.cn: 用于习惯时，它可以礼貌地把习惯说得比实际更稀少。

abstract.en: Occasionally is the word for the pattern that has no pattern.
abstract.cn: 「偶尔」是给「没有规律」的规律准备的词。

abstract.en: A low-frequency word is a dimmer switch for how much the listener should worry.
abstract.cn: 低频词像一个调光开关，控制听者该担心多少。

abstract.en: The exception needs a name so that the rule can stay standing.
abstract.cn: 例外需要一个名字，规则才能继续站着。

examples.en: The system occasionally restarts on its own.
examples.cn: 系统偶尔会自行重启。

examples.en: Occasionally, the lake freezes over completely.
examples.cn: 偶尔，湖面会完全封冻。

examples.en: She occasionally writes to the local paper.
examples.cn: 她偶尔给当地报纸投稿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「偶开胜利」——偶尔才开一次，不是常常

root: 拉丁语动词「落下」加表示「朝向」的前缀构成「落到……上、发生」，名词指落到脚边的时机；英语经法语借入名词并派生形容词「偶尔的」，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate low frequency, the sentence-opening frame, irregular intervals, relaxed speech, technical sporadicity, deliberate understatement, exception marking and older formal prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理低频、句首框架、不规则间隔、轻松口语、技术上的偶发、有意轻描淡写、标出例外，以及旧式书面用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar with a few small circles and mostly empty days.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上零星画着几个小圈，多数日子空白。

branches.en: THE LOW RATE: less often than sometimes.
branches.cn: 低频率：比「有时」更少。

branches.en: THE UNEVEN PATTERN: the opening frame and the irregular interval.
branches.cn: 不均匀的模式：句首框架与不规则间隔。

branches.en: THE SOFT HABIT: the relaxed spoken way to describe a loose routine.
branches.cn: 柔和的习惯：口语中描述松散日常的方式。

branches.en: THE MANAGED CLAIM: technical sporadicity and deliberate understatement.
branches.cn: 被管理的说法：技术上的偶发与有意的轻描淡写。

branches.en: THE EXCEPTION: a departure from the rule, and the older formal tone.

intro.en: Occasionally is a Latin towards-prefix, a falling-root, a noun of occasion, an English adjective and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「朝向」前缀、「落下」词根、表「时机」的名词、英语形容词与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The root cadere is about falling; the prefixed verb names what falls upon a person, and the noun turns that into an occasion.
latinIntro.cn: 词根的核心是「落下」；加前缀的动词指落到某人身上的事，名词再把它变成「时机」。

items.example: The prefix points the falling toward a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「落下」指向某人。

items.example: The verb gives the family its image of an event arriving.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为词族提供「事件降临」的意象。

items.example: The compound verb covers both happening and the setting sun.
items.exampleCN: 合成动词既指「发生」，也指「日落」。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of occurrence.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成表「发生之事」的名词。

items.example: The noun names the chance that happens to arrive.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指恰好到来的机会。

items.example: English borrows the noun through French.
items.exampleCN: 英语经法语借入这个名词。

items.example: The adjective shifts the noun from an event to a frequency.
items.exampleCN: 形容词把名词从「事件」转向「频率」。

items.example: The philosophical noun keeps the idea of events falling on each occasion.
items.exampleCN: 这一哲学名词保留「每次场合事件降临」的观念。

items.example: The suffix turns occasional into a frequency adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成频率副词。

scene: 历史学家在旧档案里读到，这座城曾被外来军队控制多年。The archive shows that the city lived through a long occupation.
sceneCN: 这里 occupation 指「军事占领」（第 2 个义项：以武力控制并驻守某地）；句意为档案显示这座城市经历了一段漫长的占领时期。图中可辨识物件：军旗、检查站、旧地图、档案盒；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A job or profession
senses.definition: the work a person does regularly to earn a living
senses.definitionCN: 一个人为谋生而长期从事的工作
senses.example: Her occupation is listed as laboratory technician.
senses.exampleCN: 她的职业登记为实验室技术员。
senses.why: a job takes up a person's time and attention, so the Latin verb for seizing a place was applied to seizing a day.
senses.whyCN: 工作会占去人的时间与精力，于是拉丁语中「占据地方」的动词被用来指「占去一天」。

senses.title: Military seizure and control of a place
senses.definition: the act of taking control of a country or region by armed force and staying there
senses.definitionCN: 以武力夺取并驻守控制某国或某地区的行为
senses.example: The museum closed during the occupation and lost part of its collection.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆在占领期间关闭，部分藏品散失。
senses.why: the core meaning is seizing and holding, which is exactly what an army does to a territory.
senses.whyCN: 核心义就是「夺取并占住」，这正是一支军队对一片土地所做的事。

senses.title: The act of filling or using a space
senses.definition: the act of taking up and using a building, room or piece of land
senses.definitionCN: 占用并使用某栋建筑、房间或一块土地的行为
senses.example: Occupation of the new wing begins in September.
senses.exampleCN: 新侧楼的启用入住从九月开始。
senses.why: from holding a territory to holding a room is a short step: in both cases something is taken and kept.
senses.whyCN: 从占住一片土地到占住一个房间只差一步：两件事都是「拿下来并保持住」。

senses.title: The state of being busy
senses.definition: the condition of being busy or having one's attention fully taken up
senses.definitionCN: 忙于某事、注意力被完全占去的状态
senses.example: He found occupation for his hands in repairing the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠修篱笆让双手有事可做。
senses.why: the same verb can mean to keep someone busy, and the noun records that state of being taken up.
senses.whyCN: 同一动词也可表示「使人忙于某事」，名词便记录这种被占满的状态。

senses.title: Lawful possession of property
senses.definition: the legal holding or tenancy of land or buildings
senses.definitionCN: 对土地或建筑的合法持有或租用
senses.example: The tenant's occupation of the flat is protected by statute.
senses.exampleCN: 租客对该公寓的占有受法规保护。
senses.why: property law uses the word for the fact of holding premises, whether by owner or tenant.
senses.whyCN: 财产法用这个词指持有房屋这一事实，无论持有者是业主还是租客。

senses.title: A pastime that fills the time
senses.definition: an activity pursued for interest rather than for pay
senses.definitionCN: 出于兴趣而非报酬从事的活动
senses.example: Gardening is his favourite occupation on free afternoons.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺是他空闲下午最喜爱的消遣。
senses.why: because occupation means whatever takes up one's time, it covers unpaid hobbies as well as paid work.
senses.whyCN: 既然 occupation 指「占去时间的事」，它自然既包括有薪工作，也包括无偿爱好。

senses.title: Settlement of land by newcomers
senses.titleCN: 外来者对土地的定居占用
senses.definition: the settling and use of land by people who move onto it, often without formal title
senses.definitionCN: 迁入者定居并使用土地，常无正式产权
senses.example: Early occupation of the riverbank was informal and unrecorded.
senses.exampleCN: 河岸早期的占用是非正式的，也没有记录。
senses.why: history uses the word for land taken and held by settlers, keeping the original idea of seizure.
senses.whyCN: 历史叙述用这个词指移居者取得并占住的土地，保留了「夺取」的原义。

senses.title: Something that fills the mind
senses.definition: a thought, worry or interest that takes up one's mind
senses.definitionCN: 占去心思的想法、忧虑或兴趣
senses.example: The unfinished novel became his constant occupation.
senses.exampleCN: 那部未完成的小说成了他时刻挂心的事。
senses.why: the abstract sense treats the mind as a space that can be taken and held like a city.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把心灵当作一块可以像城池一样被占据、被守住的空地。

intro.en: Occupation comes from Latin occupatio, from occupare 'to seize, take possession of', built on ob- 'against, over' and capere 'to take, grasp'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: occupation 来自拉丁 occupatio，源自动词 occupare「夺取、占有」，由 ob-「对着、在上」与 capere「拿、抓」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Capere meant 'to take, seize, grasp'. The Indo-European base often cited for it is a reconstruction, and related forms appear across the Italic languages.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿、夺取、抓」。常为其引用的印欧语词基属于重构形式，相关形态在意大利语族各语言中均有出现。

items.en: Ob- 'against, over' plus capere produced occupare 'to seize, take possession of, keep busy'.
items.cn: ob-「对着、在上」加 capere 构成 occupare「夺取、占有、使忙碌」。

items.en: The noun occupatio named the act of seizing and, by extension, whatever takes up one's time or attention.
items.cn: 名词 occupatio 指夺取行为，并引申指占去时间或注意力的事物。

items.en: Old French occupacion brought the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of holding a place or a post.
items.cn: 古法语 occupacion 在十四世纪把该词带入英语，最初指占住一个地方或职位。

items.en: War reporting fixed the military sense, while property law kept the older sense of lawful holding of premises.
items.cn: 战地报道固定了军事义，财产法则保留了「合法持有房屋」的旧义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin shape of capere is reconstructed, and the exact force of ob- in this compound is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：capere 的拉丁语前形态属于重构形式，ob- 在该复合词中的确切作用仍有争论。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same Latin verb where the ending decides the meaning; group two holds words for the work someone does.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁动词、靠词尾区分意义的词形；第二组是表示「所从事的工作」的词。

entries.definition: To take and hold a place, fill a space or keep someone busy; the noun occupation is its action form.
entries.definitionCN: 指占据并保有某地、占满空间或使人忙碌；名词 occupation 是它的行为形式。

entries.definition: The person who is in and using a place at a given time, not the job that person does.
entries.definitionCN: 指某时正在使用某处的人，而不是此人所做的职业。

entries.definition: The state or rate of a place being used, as in hotel occupancy; it measures filling, not employment.
entries.definitionCN: 指某处被使用的状态或比率，如酒店入住率；衡量的是占用，不是就业。

entries.definition: Pre- 'beforehand' plus occupied: whose attention was taken up in advance, hence absent-minded.
entries.definitionCN: pre-「事先」加 occupied：注意力事先已被占去，因此显得心不在焉。

entries.definition: A job requiring specialised training and often a formal qualification, such as law or medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 需要专门训练、通常有正式资格的职位，如法律或医学。

entries.definition: The whole course of a person's working life, viewed as a progression rather than one job.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人整个工作历程，被看作递进过程而非单一职位。

entries.definition: The state of having paid work, or the work itself; it stresses the employer relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有有薪工作的状态或该工作本身，强调雇佣关系。

entries.definition: A skilled craft or manual occupation, such as carpentry, often learned through apprenticeship.
entries.definitionCN: 指需要手艺的行业或体力职业，如木工，常通过学徒制习得。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real legal and military phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实法律与军事短语、真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ob- 'over' + capere 'seize': to seize and hold, whether a city, a room or a whole day.
normal.cn: ob-「在上」+ capere「抓取」：抓住并占住，无论是一座城、一间屋还是一整天。

normal.en: The family runs occupy, occupant, occupancy, occupation, occupational.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 occupy、occupant、occupancy、occupation、occupational。

normal.en: The job sense survives in forms asking for your occupation at the bank or the clinic.
normal.cn: 职业义仍活在银行或诊所让你填写职业的表格里。

normal.en: Military phrases keep the original force: occupation forces, under occupation.
normal.cn: 军事短语保留了原义的力量：占领军、处于占领之下。

normal.en: Property law says occupation of the premises for the fact of holding a building.
normal.cn: 财产法用 occupation of the premises 指持有房屋这一事实。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pulled up to a desk and never moved, holding the same person for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一把拉到桌前的椅子多年不动，一直占着同一个人。

abstract.en: Picture a flag planted on a hill, and the ground beneath it is no longer freely entered.
abstract.cn: 想象一面插在山头的旗，旗下的土地从此不再可自由进入。

abstract.en: Picture a single idea sitting in a room of the mind and refusing to leave.
abstract.cn: 想象一个念头坐在心灵的某个房间里，不肯离开。

examples.en: Please state your name, age and occupation on the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格上填写姓名、年龄和职业。

examples.en: The occupation lasted seven years and ended with a treaty.
examples.cn: 占领持续了七年，以一项条约结束。

examples.en: Reading was her only occupation during the long recovery.
examples.cn: 在漫长的康复期间，阅读是她唯一的消遣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oc（一再）+ cup（杯子）+ ation」——一只杯子被反复占住 → 占据、职业

root: 拉丁 ob-「对着、在上」+ capere「抓取」→ occupare「夺取、占有」→ occupatio「占据；职业」。capere 的拉丁语前形态为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of seizing and holding: an army holds a country, a tenant holds a flat, a job holds a day, a hobby holds an afternoon, and finally a thought holds the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「夺取并占住」这一动作展开：军队占住国家，租客占住公寓，职业占去一天，爱好占去一个下午，最后是一个念头占住心灵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing over a place and not letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢在一处地方上，不再松开。

branches.en: TAKING AND HOLDING LAND: armies and settlers both seize ground and stay on it.
branches.cn: 夺取并占住土地：军队与移居者都夺取地面并留在上面。

branches.en: HOLDING PREMISES: a room or a building can be occupied, lawfully or merely in fact.
branches.cn: 持有房屋：房间或建筑可以被占用，或合法，或仅成事实。

branches.en: WORK AS TAKING TIME: a job is what regularly takes up the greater part of the day.
branches.cn: 工作即占去时间：职业就是经常占去一天中大部分时间的事。

branches.en: FILLING TIME: being busy and pursuing a pastime are the same filling seen with and without pay.
branches.cn: 填满时间：忙碌与消遣是同一个「填满」，只是一个有报酬、一个没有。

branches.en: MIND AS TERRITORY: an idea can occupy the mind the way a garrison occupies a town.
branches.cn: 心灵即疆域：一个念头占据心灵，正如驻军占据城镇。

intro.en: Occupation is a Latin verb turned into an action noun: a prefix of direction, a root meaning 'seize', and a noun ending that English still uses productively.
intro.cn: occupation 是拉丁动词变来的行为名词：表方向的前缀、意为「抓取」的词根，以及英语仍能产的名称词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere supplies occupy, occupation, occupant, occupancy, capture, captive and capable; ob- adds direction or intensity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 capere 衍生 occupy、occupation、occupant、occupancy、capture、captive 与 capable；ob- 增添方向或强度。

items.example: The prefix directs the action at an object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向某个对象。

items.structure: capere, cepi, captum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root supplies the image of a closed hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「手握紧」的意象。

items.example: Legions could occupy a whole valley.
items.exampleCN: 军团能够占住整条山谷。

items.meaning: the act or result of an action
items.example: The ending turns the verb into the name of an act.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成动作的名称。

items.meaning: seizing, holding, or the work one does
items.meaningCN: 占据、持有，或所从事的工作
items.example: The word covers both holding and working.
items.exampleCN: 这个词兼指「占住」与「工作」。

items.meaning: to hold or fill a place
items.example: Two families occupy the upper floor.
Occupancy fell after the new road opened.
items.exampleCN: 新路开通后入住率下降。

items.meaningCN: 心事重重的；心不在焉的
items.example: He seemed preoccupied during the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 他在会上显得心不在焉。

senses.title: Seize and hold: take possession
senses.definition: to take possession of a place or thing and keep control of it
senses.definitionCN: 取得对某地或某物的占有，并保持控制
senses.example: The troops occupied the fort before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 部队在黎明前占领了要塞。
senses.why: Latin occupare was an emphatic form of ob 'over' plus capere 'to grasp, seize'. The core picture is a hand closing over something and not letting go.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 occupare 是 ob“覆在……之上”加 capere“抓、夺”的强调形式。核心画面就是一只手合拢抓住东西，不再放开。

senses.title: Take up space: fill a surface
senses.titleCN: 占去空间：铺满一块地方
senses.definition: to fill or cover an area of space, so that little room is left
senses.definitionCN: 填满或覆盖一块空间，几乎不留余地
senses.example: The piano occupies one corner of the living room.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴占了客厅的一个角落。
senses.why: A thing that holds a place holds it in the same grip: the floor under it is no longer free. Possession becomes measurement of space.
senses.whyCN: 占住一个位置的东西用的是同一个“握”：它下面的地板不再空着。占有于是变成对空间的度量。

senses.title: Take up time: fill a period
senses.titleCN: 占去时间：填满一段时间
senses.definition: to use up a period of time, leaving it unavailable for anything else
senses.definitionCN: 用掉一段时间，使其无法再做别的事
senses.example: The hearing occupied the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 听证会占了整整一个下午。
senses.why: Hours can be held just as floors can: once a period is gripped by an activity, it cannot be handed to another.
senses.whyCN: 小时和地板一样可以被“握住”：一段时间一旦被某项活动抓住，就无法再交给别的活动。

senses.title: Live in: hold as a home
senses.definition: to live in or use a building as one's home or base
senses.definitionCN: 住在某处，或以某建筑为住所、驻地
senses.example: The family occupies the upper floors of the building.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人住在楼的上层。
senses.why: Living somewhere is holding it continuously. The legal phrase 'occupier' grew from exactly this: the person who is in possession of the property.
senses.whyCN: 住在某处就是持续地占住它。法律用语 occupier 正由此而来：实际占有该房产的人。

senses.title: Hold an office, post or rank
senses.titleCN: 担任职位：占住一个位置
senses.definition: to hold a job, office or official position
senses.definitionCN: 担任某项工作、职务或正式职位
senses.example: She occupies the chair of the department.
senses.exampleCN: 她担任系主任一职。
senses.why: A post is a place in an institution; whoever holds it fills that slot. The space sense turns social: the seat is taken by a person.
senses.whyCN: 职位是机构里的一个位置，谁担任就由谁填进那个格子。空间义转向社会意义：座位被人占住了。

senses.title: Occupy the mind: keep attention busy
senses.titleCN: 占据心思：让注意力忙个不停
senses.definition: to fill someone's thoughts or attention, especially for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 填满某人的思绪或注意力，尤指持续很久
senses.example: The question occupied him for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题盘踞在他心里好几周。
senses.why: Attention is another space. When a thought grips it, no other thought can get in, so occupy comes to mean 'absorb the mind'.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是另一种空间。当一个念头抓住它，别的念头就进不来，于是 occupy 表示“占据心思”。

senses.title: Military occupation: control without annexing
senses.titleCN: 军事占领：控制而不并入
senses.definition: to control a country or territory with armed force, usually without making it part of one's own state
senses.definitionCN: 以武力控制某国或某地区，通常不把它并入本国
senses.example: The army occupied the region for six years.
senses.exampleCN: 军队占领该地区六年。
senses.why: The oldest 'seize' sense scaled up to whole territories. Holding the ground is the point, and the legal status of the land is left open.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的“夺取”义放大到整片领土。要点在于握住土地，而土地的法律归属则悬置不论。

senses.title: Take a place in a ranking or order
senses.definition: to have or fill a particular place in a list, ranking or sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在名单、排名或序列中占有某个位置
senses.example: The novel occupies third place on the bestseller list.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说在畅销榜上位居第三。
senses.why: A rank is a numbered slot. The thing that holds that slot occupies it, even though nothing physical is gripped.
senses.whyCN: 名次是一个带编号的格子。占住该格子的东西就 occupy 它，尽管并没有任何实体被抓住。

senses.title: Occupy oneself: keep oneself busy
senses.titleCN: 使自己忙碌：给自己找事做
senses.definition: in the reflexive form occupy oneself with, to keep oneself busy with an activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于反身形式 occupy oneself with，表示让自己忙于某项活动
senses.example: He occupied himself with repairing the old clock.
senses.exampleCN: 他让自己忙着修那口旧钟。
senses.why: The reflexive turns the grip inward: instead of an outside thing holding you, you give your own time to an activity.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把“握”转向自身：不是外物抓住你，而是你把自己的时间交给一项活动。

senses.title: Archaic euphemism: have sex with
senses.titleCN: 古委婉语：与……发生性关系
senses.definition: in 16th and 17th century usage, a polite cover for having sexual intercourse with someone
senses.definitionCN: 在 16、17 世纪用法中，作为“与某人发生性关系”的委婉说法
senses.example: Renaissance writers used occupy as a discreet cover for a sexual act.
senses.exampleCN: 文艺复兴时期的作家用 occupy 隐晦地指代性行为。
senses.why: The 'take possession of a person' sense was pushed into sexual meaning in the early 15th century. Because of that, polite usage dropped the word for a time, and occupant could even mean a prostitute.
senses.whyCN: “占有一个人的身体”这一层在 15 世纪早期被推成性含义。正因如此，讲究礼貌的用法一度回避这个词，occupant 甚至可指妓女。

intro.en: Occupy arrived in English in the mid-14th century through Old French, from Latin occupare 'seize, take possession'. The ending is hard to explain, but the record is old; a 16th-17th century sexual euphemism later pushed the word out of polite use for a while.
intro.cn: occupy 于 14 世纪中期经古法语进入英语，来自拉丁语 occupare“夺取、占有”。词尾音节难以解释，但记录已很古老；16 至 17 世纪的性委婉义后来又使这个词一度退出礼貌用法。

items.en: Occupien is recorded meaning 'to take possession of and retain or keep'; the same period shows the senses 'fill space or time' and 'employ a person'.
items.cn: occupien 记录为“取得并保有、占住”；同一时期还出现“占据空间或时间”和“雇用某人”的义项。

items.en: Borrowed irregularly from Old French ocuper / occuper (13c.), or taken directly from Latin occupare.
items.cn: 不规则地借自古法语 ocuper / occuper（13 世纪），或直接取自拉丁语 occupare。

items.en: Latin occupare 'take over, seize, take into possession' is an emphatic form of ob 'over' plus capere 'to grasp, seize'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 occupare“接管、夺取、占为己有”是 ob“覆于其上”加 capere“抓、夺”的强调形式。

items.en: Capere goes back to PIE *kap- 'to grasp', the root behind captive and capture as well.
items.cn: capere 追溯到原始印欧语 *kap-“抓”，captive 与 capture 也出自这个词根。

items.en: The sense 'have sexual intercourse with' is found from the early 15th century and served as a euphemism in the 16th and 17th centuries; Shakespeare uses it in Henry IV, Part 2, and occupant could then mean a prostitute.
items.cn: “与……发生性关系”义自 15 世纪早期可见，16、17 世纪成为委婉语；莎士比亚在《亨利四世下篇》用过它，当时的 occupant 还可指妓女。

items.en: Modern English keeps the neutral senses of holding space, time, office and attention, and forms occupation, occupant and occupancy from the same stem.
items.cn: 现代英语保留占据空间、时间、职位与注意力等中性义，并由同一词干构成 occupation、occupant、occupancy。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to happen or come to mind. It shares the ob- beginning but comes from currere 'to run', not from capere 'to seize'.
entries.definitionCN: 发生；想到。它同样以 ob- 开头，但词根是 currere“跑”，不是 capere“抓”。

entries.definition: a person who lives in or uses a place. It is the noun built on occupy, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 居住者；占用者。它是 occupy 派生的名词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: absorbed in one's own thoughts. The pre- 'before' adds the idea of the mind being taken up in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 心事重重的；出神的。pre-“预先”加了“心思先被占去”的意思。

entries.definition: to take hold of something suddenly and by force. It stresses the grab, while occupy stresses keeping possession.
entries.definitionCN: 突然用力抓住。它强调抓的动作，occupy 强调占住不放。

entries.definition: to live in a place as its population. It is used of people and animals, while occupy can also mean simply filling space.
entries.definitionCN: 作为居民住在某地。它多用于人和动物，occupy 也可仅指占据空间。

entries.definition: to attract and hold someone's interest. It focuses on the attraction, while occupy focuses on the attention being filled up.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引并保持某人的兴趣。它侧重吸引力，occupy 侧重注意力被填满。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin ob plus capere, the capere family in capture and captive, and the modern nouns occupation and occupant.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁成分 ob + capere，capture 与 captive 中的 capere 词族，以及现代名词 occupation 与 occupant。

normal.en: ob 'over' plus capere 'to grasp' gives 'grasp over something': the hand closes on it and holds.
normal.cn: ob“覆于其上”加 capere“抓”就是“在上面抓住”：手合拢握住不放。

normal.en: Capture and captive share the same capere root, so all three words are about a grip that does not let go.
normal.cn: capture 与 captive 同出 capere，因此这三个词都围绕“握住不放”。

normal.en: Obtain uses tenere 'to hold', occur uses currere 'to run': same ob- prefix, three different roots.
normal.cn: obtain 用 tenere“握持”，occur 用 currere“跑”：同一个 ob- 前缀，三个不同词根。

normal.en: Occupation is both a job and a military takeover, because both are a held place.
normal.cn: occupation 既是职业也是军事占领，因为两者都是“占住的位置”。

normal.en: Occupy oneself with is the reflexive branch: you give your own time to a task.
normal.cn: occupy oneself with 是反身分支：你把自己的时间交给一项任务。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed flat on a table: the table under it is no longer free, and that is occupy in one gesture.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌平压在桌面上：掌下的桌面不再空着，这就是 occupy 的一个动作。

abstract.en: The same hand can close on a building, an afternoon, a chair, a rank, or a thought.
abstract.cn: 同一只手可以握住一栋楼、一个下午、一把椅子、一个名次或一个念头。

abstract.en: When the grip turns inward, the hand holds its own time: that is occupy oneself.
abstract.cn: 当这只手握向自身，它握的是自己的时间：这就是 occupy oneself。

examples.en: A single bookshelf occupied the entire wall of the small study.
examples.cn: 一个书架占满了小书房整面墙。

examples.en: Rebuilding the harbour occupied the town for three summers.
examples.cn: 重建港口让全镇忙了三个夏天。

examples.en: The reporter was occupied with verifying the source and missed the call.
examples.cn: 记者正忙着核实消息来源，错过了那通电话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥 Q 派」——奥 Q 派的人一进门就占了整间会议室 → occupy 占据、占用

root: 源自拉丁语 occupare“夺取、占有”= ob-“覆于其上、对着”+ capere“抓、夺”（PIE *kap-“抓”），核心是“抓住并占住不放”；词尾音节来源难以解释。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of occupy all start from one gesture: a hand closes over something and holds it. The same grip then measures floors, hours, homes, posts, ranks, attention and, in the oldest branch, whole territories.
sensesIntro.cn: occupy 的十个义项都从同一个动作出发：手合拢抓住某物并握住。同一只握持之手随后量出地板、小时、住所、职位、名次、注意力，以及最古老分支里的整片领土。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing over something and holding it tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢抓住某物，紧紧握住不放。

branches.en: SEIZURE: taking a thing or a whole territory by force and keeping control of it.
branches.cn: 夺取：以武力拿下一件东西或整片领土，并保持控制。

branches.en: SPACE, TIME AND HOME: the grip becomes the floor a thing covers, the hours an activity uses, and the house a family lives in.
branches.cn: 空间、时间与住所：握持变成物体覆盖的地面、活动用掉的时间，以及一家人居住的房子。

branches.en: POSITION: a post or a rank is a slot in an institution or a list, and its holder fills that slot.
branches.cn: 位置：职位或名次是机构或名单中的格子，担任者把它填满。

branches.en: BUSY MIND: attention can be gripped from outside, or handed over by oneself in the reflexive form.
branches.cn: 忙碌的心神：注意力既可以被外物抓住，也可以在反身形式里由自己交出。

branches.en: THE OLD EUPHEMISM: possessing a person was pushed into sexual meaning, a branch polite usage later abandoned.
branches.cn: 旧委婉语：“占有人”被推成性含义，这一分支后来被礼貌用法弃用。

intro.en: Occupy is Latin ob- 'over, against' plus capere 'to grasp', with the verb ending -are. English keeps the stem occup- and builds nouns with -ation, -ant, -ancy and -ier.
intro.cn: occupy 由拉丁语 ob-“覆于其上、对着”加 capere“抓”和动词词尾 -are 构成。英语保留词干 occup-，并用 -ation、-ant、-ancy、-ier 造名词。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Latin occupare, an emphatic compound of ob and capere; capere 'to grasp' is the root at the centre.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是拉丁语 occupare，即 ob 与 capere 的强调复合词；中心的词根是 capere“抓”。

items.meaning: to seize and hold; to fill space, time or attention
items.example: Two guards occupy the gate at all times.
items.exampleCN: 两名卫兵始终守着大门。

items.meaning: a person who lives in or uses a place
items.meaningCN: 居住者；占用者；乘坐者（-ant 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The new occupant moved in last Friday.
items.exampleCN: 新住户上周五搬了进来。

items.meaning: the state of being occupied; the rate of use
items.meaningCN: 占用；居住；入住率（-ancy 构成状态名词）
items.example: Hotel occupancy falls sharply in winter.
items.exampleCN: 旅馆入住率在冬季大幅下降。

items.meaning: a job; the act of taking control of a place
items.meaningCN: 职业；占领；占用（-ation 构成行为或状态名词）
items.exampleCN: 她把自己的职业填作“译者”。

items.meaning: relating to a job or the workplace
items.meaningCN: 职业的；职业引起的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Noise is a common occupational hazard in factories.
items.exampleCN: 噪音是工厂里常见的职业危害。

items.meaning: the person who occupies a property or territory
items.example: The occupier of the flat is responsible for repairs.
items.exampleCN: 该公寓的住户负责维修。

items.meaning: absorbed in one's own thoughts; already taken up
items.meaningCN: 心事重重的；专注的（pre-“预先”+ occupy，心思先被占去）
items.example: He was too preoccupied to notice the rain.
items.exampleCN: 他心事太重，没注意到下雨。

items.meaning: a thought or subject that fills the mind
items.meaningCN: 全神贯注的事；心头大事
items.exampleCN: 安全成了他心头最挂念的事。

items.structure: capt- (grasp, from capere) + -ure (noun and verb ending)
items.meaning: to take by force or to record an image
items.example: The camera captured the whole scene.

items.meaningCN: 被关押的；俘虏（同一“抓”词根）
items.example: The captive birds were released at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 被关的鸟在黎明时被放走了。

senses.title: Run to meet: the Latin core sense
senses.titleCN: 迎面跑去：拉丁语的本义
senses.definition: in the original Latin sense, to run toward something and meet it, including meeting an opponent in argument
senses.definitionCN: 按拉丁语本义，跑向某物并与之相遇，也包括在争论中迎上对手
senses.example: Latin occurrere described two people or things running toward each other until they met.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁语 occurrere 描述两方在奔跑中相互靠近，直到碰上。
senses.why: Latin occurrere joined ob 'against, toward' to currere 'to run'. The first picture is a head-on meeting, not an accident and not a thought.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 occurrere 把 ob“迎着、朝着”与 currere“跑”组合起来。最初的画面是迎面相遇，既不是事故，也不是念头。

senses.title: Happen: take place
senses.definition: to happen, especially without being planned or looked for
senses.definitionCN: 发生，尤指并非计划之中或特意寻找的
senses.example: The accident occurred at the crossroads just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 事故就发生在午夜过后的十字路口。
senses.why: From 'meet' the word moved to 'present itself in the course of events'. An event that meets you on the road is an event that happens to you.
senses.whyCN: 从“相遇”出发，这个词转向“在事件进程中自己浮现”。在路上迎上你的事，就是发生在你身上的事。

senses.title: Happen at a stated time or place
senses.definition: to take place at a particular point in time or in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 在特定的时间点或特定地点发生
senses.example: The festival occurs in the first week of June.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日在六月的第一周举行。
senses.why: Once an event is pictured as meeting you, it can be pinned to a spot on the road and a moment on the clock.
senses.whyCN: 一旦事件被想象成与你相遇，它就能被钉在路上的某个地点和时钟上的某个时刻。

senses.title: Be found to exist: occur in nature
senses.titleCN: 存在于某处：自然界里有它
senses.definition: to be found or to exist in a place, a group, or a natural setting
senses.definitionCN: 在某地、某群体或自然环境中被发现、存在
senses.example: This orchid occurs only in the high wetlands of the north.
senses.exampleCN: 这种兰花只生长在北部的髙地湿地。
senses.why: If a thing presents itself when you go looking, it 'occurs' there: the meeting becomes a record of where it can be met.
senses.whyCN: 如果去找就能遇见，它就是“occur”在那里：相遇变成了“何处能遇见它”的记录。

senses.title: Appear in a text or a list
senses.definition: to appear in a piece of writing, a list, or a set of data
senses.definitionCN: 出现在文章、名单或一组数据中
senses.example: The word 'harbour' occurs four times in the first paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: harbour 这个词在第一段出现了四次。
senses.why: A page is a road too: the reader runs along it, and every word that meets the eye 'occurs' at that point.
senses.whyCN: 书页也是一条路：读者沿着它跑，每一个撞进眼睛的词就在那一点“occur”。

senses.title: Come into the mind: occur to someone
senses.definition: in the pattern occur to someone, of an idea: to come into a person's mind
senses.definitionCN: 用于 occur to someone 结构，指想法进入某人脑中
senses.example: It never occurred to me to check the date on the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 我从没想到要去核对信上的日期。
senses.why: The 1620s added the mental branch: a thought runs toward you and meets you, seemingly from outside, which is why English says the idea occurred rather than 'I thought it'.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 20 年代增加了心理分支：一个念头朝你跑来并遇上你，好像来自外部，所以英语说“想法 occur 了”，而不是“我想到了它”。

senses.title: Exist in a particular form or variety
senses.definition: to exist in a particular form, type, or variety, often one of several
senses.definitionCN: 以某种形态、类型或变体存在，常是若干种之一
senses.example: The mineral occurs in two distinct crystal forms.
senses.exampleCN: 这种矿物以两种不同的晶体形态存在。
senses.why: The 'be met with' sense narrows to how a thing is met: the form it presents when you encounter it.
senses.whyCN: “能被遇见”的义项收窄为“以何种样子被遇见”：你碰到它时它呈现的形态。

senses.title: Occur to someone to do: an idea that prompts action
senses.titleCN: 想到要去做：推动行动的念头
senses.definition: in the pattern it occurs to someone to do something, of an idea that suggests an action
senses.definitionCN: 用于 「it occurs to someone to do something」 结构，指想到该做某事
senses.example: It occurred to her to call the police before leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开前想到该报警。
senses.why: The mental meeting can carry a plan as well as a fact: what meets the mind is not only 'that something is so' but 'that something should be done'.
senses.whyCN: 心理上的相遇既能带来事实，也能带来计划：撞进脑子的不只是“事情如此”，还有“应该去做”。

intro.en: Occur entered English in the 1520s meaning 'meet, meet in argument', from Latin occurrere 'run to meet'. The sense 'happen' and the mental sense 'come into the mind' followed within a century.
intro.cn: occur 于 16 世纪 20 年代进入英语，意为“相遇、在争论中迎上”，来自拉丁语 occurrere“跑去相遇”。“发生”义与“想到”义在一个世纪内相继出现。

items.en: First recorded meaning 'meet, meet in argument', with the physical head-on meeting still visible in the word.
items.cn: 最早记录为“相遇、在争论中迎上”，词里仍看得见那种物理性的迎面相遇。

items.en: From French occurrer 'happen unexpectedly', or directly from Latin occurrere.
items.cn: 来自法语 occurrer“意外发生”，或直接来自拉丁语 occurrere。

items.en: Latin occurrere 'run to meet, run against, befall, present itself' is ob 'against, toward' plus currere 'to run'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 occurrere“跑去相遇、迎面撞上、降临、自己出现”由 ob“迎着、朝向”加 currere“跑”构成。

items.en: Currere goes back to PIE *kers- 'to run', the root also seen in current and excursion.
items.cn: currere 追溯到原始印欧语 *kers-“跑”，current 与 excursion 也出自这个词根。

items.en: The noun occurrence is recorded from the 1530s; the sense 'come into one's mind' appears in the 1620s.
items.cn: 名词 occurrence 自 16 世纪 30 年代有记录；“想到”义出现于 17 世纪 20 年代。

items.en: Modern English keeps the event sense as the main one and leaves the literal meeting to the root; occurrence, co-occur and recur carry the family forward.
items.cn: 现代英语以事件义为主，把字面的“相遇”留在词根里；occurrence、co-occur、recur 延续了这个词族。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to fill space, time or attention. It shares oc-/ob- and the -py ending shape but comes from capere 'to grasp', not currere 'to run'.
entries.definitionCN: 占据空间、时间或注意力。它形似 occur，但词根是 capere“抓”，不是 currere“跑”。

entries.definition: an event, or the fact of something happening. It is the noun from occur, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 事件；发生。它是 occur 派生的名词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: to happen again. It uses re- 'again' plus the same currere 'to run' root.
entries.definitionCN: 再次发生。它用 re-“再次”加同一个 currere“跑”词根。

entries.definition: to take place, usually by chance. It is the plain everyday word, while occur is more formal and often written.
entries.definitionCN: 发生，通常带偶然意味。它是最平实的日常词，occur 更正式，多用于书面。

entries.definition: to happen or become known. It is formal and often suggests that facts emerged gradually.
entries.definitionCN: 发生；逐渐为人所知。它偏正式，常暗示事实慢慢显露。

entries.definition: to come into being, especially of problems or situations. It points to a source, while occur only records that something took place.
entries.definitionCN: 产生，尤指问题或局面。它指向来源，occur 只记录某事发生了。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin ob plus currere, the currere family in current and excursion, and the fixed pattern occur to someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁成分 ob + currere，current 与 excursion 中的 currere 词族，以及固定结构 occur to someone。

normal.en: ob 'toward' plus currere 'to run' gives 'run to meet': something comes at you and you meet it.
normal.cn: ob“朝向”加 currere“跑”就是“跑去相遇”：有东西朝你而来，你与它撞上。

normal.en: Current, excursion, concur and recur all share currere 'to run', the root that makes occur a meeting.
normal.cn: current、excursion、concur、recur 都含 currere“跑”，正是这个词根让 occur 成为一次相遇。

normal.en: Obtain uses tenere 'to hold' and occupy uses capere 'to grasp': the same ob- prefix, three different roots.
normal.cn: obtain 用 tenere“握持”，occupy 用 capere“抓”：同一个 ob- 前缀，三个不同词根。

normal.en: It never occurred to me is the mental branch: the idea runs up to you from outside.
normal.cn: it never occurred to me 是心理分支：念头从外面跑到你面前。

normal.en: Occurrence, co-occur and recur are the everyday nouns and verbs built on the same stem.
normal.cn: occurrence、co-occur、recur 是由同一词干构成的日常名词和动词。

abstract.en: Picture two runners on one road, each heading straight for the other: that collision is the original occur.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条路上两个奔跑的人，各自直冲对方：那次相撞就是 occur 的原型。

abstract.en: An event can run at you the same way, which is why a fault or an accident 'occurs' rather than simply being there.
abstract.cn: 事件也能以同样的方式朝你跑来，所以故障或事故是“occur”，而不只是“在那里”。

abstract.en: A thought can run at you too: it appears from outside, meets the mind, and is reported as occurred.
abstract.cn: 念头也会朝你跑来：它从外面出现，撞上你的心，被说成“occur 了”。

examples.en: Most errors in the survey occurred where the form was printed in two columns.
examples.cn: 问卷中的大多数错误发生在表格排成两栏的地方。

examples.en: It occurred to him only later that the key had been left in the door.
examples.cn: 他后来才想到钥匙被留在了门上。

examples.en: These fish occur in every river along the coast.
examples.cn: 这种鱼在沿海每条河里都有分布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，扣儿」——哦，扣儿！扣子突然掉了，事情就这样发生了 → occur 发生、出现

root: 源自拉丁语 occurrere“跑去相遇、迎面撞上”= ob-“迎着、朝向”+ currere“跑”（PIE *kers-“跑”），核心是“朝你跑来并撞见”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of occur all start from one picture: something runs toward you on the same road. The meeting then becomes an event, a location, a line in a text, a form in nature, and finally an idea that arrives in the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: occur 的八个义项都从同一幅画出发：有东西在同一条路上朝你跑来。那次相遇随后变成事件、地点、文本里的一行、自然界中的一种形态，最后变成抵达脑中的念头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something running toward you on the same road until it meets you.
core.cn: 核心意象：有东西在同一条路上朝你跑来，直到与你相遇。

branches.en: THE LITERAL MEETING: the Latin head-on encounter, including meeting an opponent in argument.
branches.cn: 字面的相遇：拉丁语里的迎面撞见，也包括争论中迎上对手。

branches.en: THE EVENT: what presents itself in the course of things, and can be pinned to a time and place.
branches.cn: 事件：在事情进程中自己出现的东西，可以被钉在某个时间与地点。

branches.en: THE FOUND THING: where a species or mineral can be met, and in what form it presents itself.
branches.cn: 被遇见之物：物种或矿物能在何处遇到，以及它以什么形态出现。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN PAGE: the road becomes a text, and each word meets the reader at a point.
branches.cn: 书页：路变成文本，每个词在某个位置与读者相遇。

branches.en: THE MIND: an idea runs up to you, either as a fact noticed or as an action suggested.
branches.cn: 心念：念头跑到你面前，或者作为一个被注意到的事实，或者作为一件该做的事。

intro.en: Occur is Latin ob- 'toward, against' plus currere 'to run', with the verb ending -ere. English keeps the stem occurr- and adds -ence, -ent and the prefixes co- and re-.
intro.cn: occur 由拉丁语 ob-“迎着、朝向”加 currere“跑”和动词词尾 -ere 构成。英语保留词干 occurr-，并加 -ence、-ent 以及前缀 co-、re-。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Latin occurrere, from ob and currere; currere 'to run' is the root shared by current, course and excursion.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是拉丁语 occurrere，由 ob 与 currere 构成；currere“跑”是 current、course、excursion 共有的词根。

items.meaning: to run to meet; to present itself, happen, or come to mind
items.meaningCN: 迎面相遇；出现；发生；想到
items.example: The same problem occurs in every third sample.
items.exampleCN: 每三个样本中就有一个出现同样的问题。

items.meaning: the fact of happening, or an event that happens
items.meaningCN: 发生；发生的事件（-ence 构成名词）
items.example: Power cuts are a weekly occurrence here.

items.meaning: happening at a particular time; incidental
items.meaningCN: 正在发生的；偶然发生的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: The occurrent noise came from the lift shaft.
items.exampleCN: 当时那阵声响来自电梯井。

items.meaning: to happen or appear at the same time
items.meaningCN: 同时发生；共现（co- 表“共同”）
items.example: Rain and strong wind often co-occur in this valley.
items.exampleCN: 在这个山谷里，降雨和大风常常同时出现。

items.meaning: to run back again, hence to happen once more
items.meaningCN: 再次发生；复发（re-“再次”+ currere“跑”）
items.exampleCN: 疼痛每年春天都会复发。

items.example: Doctors watch for a recurrence of the tumour.
items.exampleCN: 医生密切留意肿瘤是否复发。

items.meaning: running or flowing now; a flow of water or power
items.example: The current carries the boat downstream.

items.meaning: a running out, hence a short journey
items.meaningCN: 远足；短途旅行（ex-“出”+ currere“跑”）
items.example: The class took a one-day excursion to the coast.
items.exampleCN: 全班去海边做了一日短途旅行。

items.meaning: to run together, hence to agree or happen at once
items.meaningCN: 同时发生；同意（con-“共同”+ currere“跑”）
items.example: Both experts concur with the report's conclusion.
items.exampleCN: 两位专家都同意报告的结论。

items.meaning: to run into something, hence to bring upon oneself
items.meaningCN: 招致；蒙受（in-“进入”+ currere“跑”，即“撞上”）
items.example: Late payment will incur a fine.

latinEntries.meaning: to run to meet, run against, befall, present itself
latinEntries.meaningCN: 跑去相遇；迎面撞上；降临；自己出现

definition_zh: 发生；出现；事件；发生率；（矿物的）产出；出现次数
definition_en: the fact of something happening or existing, or an event that happens
core_image: 日历上某一天被红笔圈了一下，旁边只写了两个字：发生了。
scene: 保险报告统计过去五年同类事故的情况，发现多数集中在雨季。The report counted the occurrence of similar accidents over five years.
sceneCN: 这里 occurrence 是“同类事件发生的次数、发生情况”（第 3 个义项）；句意：报告统计了过去五年同类事故的发生次数；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 发生；出现；事件；发生率；（矿物的）产出；出现次数

derivatives.zh: 发生；出现；被想到
再次发生；复发
正在发生的；偶然发生的

senses.title: Something that happens
senses.definition: an event or incident that takes place, especially one that is noticed
senses.definitionCN: 发生的事件或事故，尤指被注意到的一次
senses.example: The police logged every unusual occurrence at the border that night.
senses.exampleCN: 警方记录了那晚边境上每一件不寻常的事。
senses.why: The word can point at the thing itself: once an event has happened, it can be counted, listed, and reported like an object.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指向事情本身：事件一旦发生，就能像物件一样被计数、列举与报告。

senses.title: The fact of happening
senses.definition: the fact or process of something happening or existing
senses.definitionCN: 某事物发生或存在的事实与过程
senses.example: The occurrence of frost in June surprised the growers.
senses.exampleCN: 六月出现霜冻让种植户感到意外。
senses.why: Here the word names not the event but its coming into being; the emphasis is on 'that it happened at all'.
senses.whyCN: 这里命名的不是事件，而是它“产生”这一过程；重点在于“它竟然发生了”。

senses.title: How often it happens
senses.titleCN: 出现次数：一段时间里发生了几回
senses.definition: the number of times something happens within a stated period or group
senses.definitionCN: 某事物在特定时段或群体内发生的次数
senses.example: The occurrence of the error fell by half after the new check was added.
senses.exampleCN: 加入新检查后，该错误的发生次数减少了一半。
senses.why: Counting turns an event into a rate; agencies need the count, not the story of any single case.
senses.whyCN: 计数把事件变成比率；机构需要的是次数，而不是任何单个案例的故事。

senses.title: A rate in statistics
senses.titleCN: 发生率：分母里的那批人
senses.definition: the proportion of a population in which a specified event happens over a period
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内，特定事件在某一群体中发生的比例
senses.example: The occurrence rate of the side effect was two cases per thousand patients.
senses.exampleCN: 该副作用的发生率为每千名患者两例。
senses.why: Statistics adds a denominator: the same number of cases means different things in a small town and a large city.
senses.whyCN: 统计学加上了分母：同样的病例数，在小镇和大城市意味着不同的事情。

senses.title: Something found in nature
senses.titleCN: 自然出现：不必人为制造
senses.definition: the presence of a substance, species, or phenomenon in the natural environment
senses.definitionCN: 某物质、物种或现象在自然环境中存在
senses.example: The natural occurrence of the mineral in local rock made mining cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 这种矿物在当地岩石中天然产出，使开采成本很低。
senses.why: The word reports existence without agency: no one made it happen, it is simply found where conditions allowed it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词报告的是“存在”而非“作为”：无人使它发生，它只是在条件允许的地方被找到。

senses.title: A mineral showing in rock
senses.titleCN: 矿点：地质图上标出的那一处
senses.definition: a deposit or showing of a mineral in a particular place, as recorded in geology
senses.definitionCN: 地质记录中某地矿物的矿床或露头
senses.example: The survey marked three occurrences of copper in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 勘测在山谷里标出了三处铜矿点。
senses.why: Geology gives the word a spatial sense: an occurrence is where the mineral 'turns up', a point on a map rather than a moment in time.
senses.whyCN: 地质学给这个词一个空间义：occurrence 是矿物“露面”的地点，是地图上的一点，而不是时间中的一刻。

senses.title: A word appearing in text
senses.titleCN: 出现：某个词在文本里露了几次
senses.definition: an instance of a linguistic item appearing in a text or corpus
senses.definitionCN: 某一语言项在文本或语料库中出现的一次实例
senses.example: The corpus records each occurrence of the phrase with its source line.
senses.exampleCN: 语料库记录该短语的每一次出现及其所在行。
senses.why: Linguistics counts tokens: every time the same form appears, it is a separate occurrence, even though the word is one.
senses.whyCN: 语言学数的是“个例”：同一形式每出现一次就是一个独立的 occurrence，尽管那个词只有一个。

senses.title: A case of disease
senses.titleCN: 病例出现：医院登记的那一例
senses.definition: a single diagnosed case of a disease in a population under surveillance
senses.definitionCN: 监测群体中被诊断出的一例疾病
senses.example: The health office reported the first occurrence of the new strain in March.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生部门报告了这种新毒株在三月首次出现。
senses.why: Public health treats each case as a countable unit; the word then means 'one more instance has entered the record'.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生把每一例当作可计数的单位；这个词于是表示“记录里又多了一例”。

intro.en: Occurrence comes from Latin occurrentia, from occurrere, to run to meet: ob- 'toward, against' plus currere 'to run'. The same verb gives occur and current.
intro.cn: occurrence 来自拉丁语 occurrentia，出自 occurrere“跑过去相遇”：ob-“朝向、对着”加 currere“跑”。同一动词给出 occur 与 current。

items.en: Currere meant to run. It underlies current, course, cursor, and excursion, all involving movement along a path.
items.cn: currere 意为跑。它构成 current、course、cursor、excursion，这些都涉及沿路径的运动。

items.en: Ob- plus currere meant to run up against something, hence to meet it, to present itself, or to come to mind.
items.cn: ob- 加 currere 意为跑上去撞见某物，因而表示相遇、浮现，或想起。

items.en: The noun named the act of meeting or turning up, and later a thing that turns up.
items.cn: 该名词指相遇或出现的行为，后来指出现的事物。

items.en: French occurrence kept the sense of an event that presents itself, especially something unexpected.
items.cn: 法语 occurrence 保留“自行出现的事件”之义，尤指意外之事。

items.en: English occurrence first meant a happening or an incident, then extended to frequency and to the presence of substances in nature.
items.cn: 英语 occurrence 最初指发生的事情或事件，随后扩展到频次，以及物质在自然中的存在。

items.en: Statistics, geology, linguistics, and medicine each gave the word a technical count: rate, deposit, token, case.
items.cn: 统计学、地质学、语言学与医学各自给这个词一个技术性计数：比率、矿点、个例、病例。

note.en: The first group is the occur family; the second compares words for things that happen, from the neutral event to the unexpected incident.
note.cn: 第一组是 occur 词族；第二组比较表示“发生之事”的词，从中性的事件到意外的变故。

entries.definition: to happen or exist; also to come into the mind. It names the event's coming about.
entries.definitionCN: 发生、存在；也指被想到；命名的是事件的发生。

entries.definition: to happen again, especially at intervals. The prefix re- adds repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 再次发生，尤指有间隔地复发；前缀 re- 增加重复义。

entries.definition: happening at a particular time; also used in philosophy for what is present.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一时刻发生的；哲学中也指当下呈现的。

entries.definition: anything that happens, especially something planned or notable. It is the broadest word.
entries.definitionCN: 发生的任何事，尤指计划中的或值得注意的；是最宽泛的词。

entries.definition: an event, often minor or unpleasant, that interrupts normal activity.
entries.definitionCN: 打断正常活动的意外事件，常较轻微或不愉快。

entries.definition: a single example or case of something general. It stresses the sample, not the happening.
entries.definitionCN: 一般事物的单个例子或案例；侧重样本，而非发生。

entries.definition: the number of times something happens in a period. It measures the count, not the event.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物在一段时间内发生的次数；测量计数，而非事件。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ob- 'against' plus currere 'to run', then -ence. Something that runs up against you has occurred.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ob-“对着”加 currere“跑”，再加 -ence。跑上来撞见你的东西，就是“发生了”。

normal.en: Occurrence is a run-in: something came along the path and met the moment.
normal.cn: occurrence 是一次撞见：某物沿路跑来，撞上了那个时刻。

normal.en: A red circle on the calendar marks one occurrence; the tally beside it counts them all.
normal.cn: 日历上的红圈标出一次 occurrence；旁边的计数把它们全数出来。

normal.en: Geology puts occurrence on a map; statistics puts it in a rate.
normal.cn: 地质学把 occurrence 放到地图上；统计学把它放进比率里。

normal.en: Every occurrence of a word in a corpus is one more token, even if the word is one.
normal.cn: 语料库里每出现一次该词就是一个新的个例，尽管那个词只有一个。

normal.en: A rare occurrence is news; a common occurrence is weather.
normal.cn: 罕见的事是新闻；常见的事是天气。

abstract.en: Occurrence is the most neutral word for change: it reports that something met the world, without saying why.
abstract.cn: occurrence 是关于变化最中性的词：它报告某物遇上了世界，却不解释原因。

abstract.en: Counting occurrences turns a story into a rate, and a rate is easier to compare than a story.
abstract.cn: 统计发生次数把故事变成比率，而比率比故事更容易比较。

abstract.en: What counts as an occurrence depends on where the observer draws the boundary of the event.
abstract.cn: 什么算作一次 occurrence，取决于观察者把事件的边界画在哪里。

examples.en: Flooding used to be a rare occurrence here, but the records now show it every other spring.
examples.cn: 这里过去很少发生洪水，但记录显示如今几乎隔年春天就有一次。

examples.en: The mineral's occurrence in the cliff was noted long before anyone tried to mine it.
examples.cn: 早在有人尝试开采之前，这种矿物在崖壁上的产出就已被记录。

examples.en: Each occurrence of the symbol in the manuscript was catalogued by hand.
examples.cn: 手稿中该符号的每一次出现都被手工编入目录。

dict_mnemonic.text: occur（发生）+ rence（名词）——发生的事、出现的次数，就是 occurrence。

root: 源自拉丁语 occurrentia，出自 occurrere“跑上去相遇”：ob-“对着”加 currere“跑”；本义为“迎面出现”，引申为“发生、事件、出现次数”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of occurrence. One idea holds them together: something turns up. It may turn up as a single event, as the fact of happening, as a count, as a rate, as a mineral in rock, as a word in a text, or as a case in a clinic.
sensesIntro.cn: occurrence 的八个义项由同一个观念维系：某物露面了。它可以是单个事件、发生这一事实、一个计数、一个比率、岩石中的矿物、文本中的词，或诊所里的一例病例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one day circled in red on a calendar, with two words beside it: it happened.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上某一天被红笔圈住，旁边写着两个字：发生了。

chain: LATIN OCCURRERE TO RUN UPON MEET
FRENCH OCCURRENCE AN EVENT THAT PRESENTS ITSELF
ENGLISH OCCURRENCE ANYTHING THAT TURNS UP

branches.en: THE THING AND THE FACT: an event that happened, and the bare fact that it happened.
branches.cn: 事情与事实：发生的事件，以及“它发生了”这一赤裸事实。

branches.en: COUNT AND RATE: how many times it turned up, and what proportion of a population it touched.
branches.cn: 次数与比率：它出现了多少回，以及它触及了群体中多大的比例。

branches.en: TURNING UP IN NATURE: a substance or species present without being made.
branches.cn: 在自然中露面：未被制造却已存在的物质或物种。

branches.en: TURNING UP IN SPACE AND TEXT: a mineral point on a map, a token in a corpus.
branches.cn: 在空间与文本中露面：地图上的矿点，语料库中的一个词例。

branches.en: TURNING UP IN THE CLINIC: one more diagnosed case entering the record.
branches.cn: 在诊所里露面：又一例确诊病例进入记录。

intro.en: Occurrence is occur plus -ence, the noun suffix for a state or an act. The family uses re- for happening again and -ent for the adjective.
intro.cn: occurrence 是 occur 加 -ence（表示状态或行为的名词后缀）。词族用 re- 表示再次发生，-ent 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is currere, to run, with ob- adding the meeting. Latin occurrere also meant to come to mind, which survives in the phrase 'it occurred to me'.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 currere“跑”，ob- 增加“相遇”之义。拉丁语 occurrere 也指“想起”，这一含义留在英语 it occurred to me 中。

items.meaning: to happen, or to come to mind
items.example: The accident occurred at the junction.

items.meaning: an event or the fact of happening
items.example: Power cuts are a daily occurrence in the old quarter.
The fever recurred after the treatment stopped.

items.meaning: a return of something after an interval
items.meaningCN: 某事物间隔一段时间后再次出现
items.example: The recurrence rate was lower in the second group.
The occurrent event was recorded but not explained.
items.exampleCN: 发生的事件被记录下来，却未得到解释。

items.example: Two concurrent storms hit the coast.
items.exampleCN: 两场风暴同时袭击了海岸。

items.meaning: a flow of water, air, or electricity; also present in time
items.meaningCN: 水流、气流或电流；也指当下的
items.example: The current carries the boat downstream.

items.meaning: the moving marker on a screen
items.example: The cursor stopped at the start of the line.

items.meaning: a short trip out and back
items.example: The class made a day excursion to the quarry.
items.exampleCN: 班级去采石场做了一日远足。

latinEntries.meaning: to run to meet, to present itself

senses.title: The world-encircling body of salt water
senses.titleCN: 覆盖地球大部分表面的连片咸水
senses.definition: the great body of salt water that surrounds the continents and covers most of the planet
senses.definitionCN: 环绕各大陆、覆盖地球大部分表面的巨大咸水体
senses.example: A single ocean can hold more water than all the land it surrounds.
senses.exampleCN: 一个海洋能容纳的水量超过它周围全部陆地。
senses.why: Greek Okeanos named the stream believed to run all the way around the world, so the word began as one continuous encircling water, not as a list of separate seas.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 Okeanos 原本指绕世界一周的大河，所以这个词从诞生起就是「一圈连着的咸水」，而非若干彼此分开的海。

senses.title: One of the named divisions
senses.titleCN: 五大洋中一个有名字的洋
senses.definition: one of the five large divisions of this water, such as the Pacific, Atlantic or Indian ocean
senses.definitionCN: 这片水域被划分出的五大洋之一，如太平洋、大西洋或印度洋
senses.example: The Atlantic ocean narrows toward its northern end.
senses.exampleCN: 大西洋在它的北端变窄。
senses.why: once geographers divided the single world water into named basins, the same word served both the whole and each part, and context decides which is meant.
senses.whyCN: 地理学家把这一整片世界水域划分成有名字的海盆之后，同一个词既指整体也指其中一部分，靠上下文决定所指。

senses.title: The water as opposed to the land
senses.definition: the open salt water thought of as a place distinct from land, especially in travel and trade
senses.definitionCN: 与陆地相对的开阔咸水，尤用于航行与贸易语境
senses.example: They spent three weeks on the ocean before sighting land.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海上待了三个星期才看见陆地。
senses.why: a voyage needs two settings, land and water; the word supplies the second one, so 'on the ocean' simply means out on the salt water.
senses.whyCN: 一次远航需要两个场景：陆地与水面；这个词提供后者，因此「在海洋上」就是身处开阔咸水之中。

senses.title: A very large amount
senses.definition: an immense quantity of something, especially something abstract such as words or work
senses.definitionCN: 某事物数量极大，尤指话语、工作等抽象事物
senses.example: An ocean of paperwork awaited the new clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 海量的文书工作等着这位新职员。
senses.why: the figurative step is simple: the largest thing most speakers know becomes the measure of anything too big to count, so an ocean of forms is just too many forms.
senses.whyCN: 比喻的跳跃很简单：把说话人知道的最大之物拿来度量多到数不清的东西，因此「一整个海洋的表格」就是表格多到数不清。

senses.title: A boundless expanse
senses.definition: a vast unbroken stretch of something that seems to have no edge, such as sand or grass
senses.definitionCN: 沙、草等铺展到看不见边界的广阔一片
senses.example: An ocean of sand stretched from the road to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 一片沙海从路边一直铺到地平线。
senses.why: the eye reads any surface without a visible edge the way it reads water, so desert and prairie borrow the word for the same feeling of no boundary.
senses.whyCN: 人眼看到没有可见边界的表面时，读法与看水面一样，因此沙漠与草原借这个词表达同样的「无边」之感。

senses.title: A depth of feeling
senses.definition: an overwhelming quantity of a feeling that seems to swallow a person up
senses.definitionCN: 铺天盖地、仿佛把人吞没的情感
senses.example: She sank into an ocean of grief after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼之后，她沉入一片悲痛的汪洋。
senses.why: deep water is the standing image for what cannot be crossed or controlled, so grief and doubt are described as oceans, with the person inside them rather than beside them.
senses.whyCN: 深水一直是无从跨越、无法掌控的意象，因此悲伤与疑虑被说成海洋，而人是在其中，不在其旁。

senses.title: The ocean as a climate system
senses.definition: the salt water regarded as a system that stores heat, moves currents and regulates the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 把咸水视为储存热量、驱动洋流并调节大气的一个系统
senses.example: The ocean absorbs much of the heat trapped by greenhouse gases.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋吸收了温室气体截留的大部分热量。
senses.why: twentieth-century earth science turned the place into a mechanism: the same water that sails are built for is now studied as a store and pump of heat.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的地球科学把这个地点变成了机制：原本造船航行的同一片水，如今被当作热量的储库与泵来研究。

senses.title: The high seas in law
senses.definition: open water beyond any state's coastal jurisdiction, belonging to no single country
senses.definitionCN: 超出任何国家沿海管辖范围、不属任何一国所有的开阔水域
senses.example: Beyond the twelve-mile limit lies the open ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 越过十二海里界限，就是开阔的公海。
senses.why: maritime law needed a term for water that no flag claims; the everyday word for the great water took that legal slot without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 海商法需要一个词指没有任何国旗主张的水域，于是日常指大水的词原样填进了这个法律位置。

senses.title: Ocean as a shipping modifier
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean carried by, used on, or belonging to the open sea
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示由远洋承运、用于远洋或属于远洋的
senses.example: Ocean freight moves most goods between continents.
senses.exampleCN: 远洋货运承担了洲际间的大部分货物。
senses.why: when a noun is placed before another noun it stops naming a place and starts naming a route or a class, which is how ocean becomes the label on a shipping container.
senses.whyCN: 名词放到另一个名词前时，它不再指地点，而开始指一条路线或一个类别，海洋就是这样变成了集装箱上的运输标签。

intro.en: Ocean reaches English through Latin and Old French from Greek Okeanos, the name of the stream that was thought to run around the whole inhabited world. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ocean 经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，源头是希腊语 Okeanos——古人想象中环绕整个已知世界的大河之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Okeanos in Homer is the river that encircles the disc of the world and is never crossed; it is a proper name first, a common noun for the outer water later.
items.cn: 荷马笔下的 Okeanos 是环绕世界圆盘、无人能越的大河；它先是专名，后来才成为指外围水域的普通名词。

items.en: Later Greek writers, above all Herodotus, used okeanos for the open water outside the Mediterranean, and the word began to mean the sea itself rather than a river.
items.cn: 后来的希腊作者，尤其是希罗多德，用 okeanos 指地中海之外的开阔水域，这个词开始表示海本身而非一条河。

items.en: Latin took Oceanus as both a name and a common noun for the great sea; the adjective oceanicus 'of the ocean' follows the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 Oceanus 同时用作专名与指大海洋的普通名词；形容词 oceanicus「海洋的」沿用同一词干。

items.en: Old French occean passed the word to Middle English around the fourteenth century, where it first named the outer sea and only later any large body of salt water.
items.cn: 古法语 occean 在 14 世纪前后把这个词传给中古英语，最初指外围的大海，后来才泛指任何巨大咸水体。

items.en: From the age of exploration the single world water was mapped as named oceans, and the older 'stream around the world' image survives only in poetry and etymology.
items.cn: 从大航海时代起，这一整片世界水域被绘制成有名字的几个大洋，古老「绕世大河」的意象只留在诗歌与词源说明里。

items.en: Source uncertain (root origin, not first date): the deeper origin of Greek Okeanos is disputed, with some scholars treating it as a pre-Greek loan; any reconstructed Indo-European form for it is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指词根来源，不是首见年代）：希腊语 Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，有学者视之为前希腊语借词；为它构拟的任何印欧语形式都只是假说，不是已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like ocean or are built on the same stem; group two holds words for water that differ in size or register.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ocean 形近或同出同一词干的词；第二组是都指水域、但规模或语体不同的词。

entries.definition: the collective name for the Pacific islands and Australia; it adds -ia to the Oceanus stem, so it names a region, not a body of water.
entries.definitionCN: 太平洋岛屿与澳大利亚的合称；在 Oceanus 词干上加 -ia，指一个区域，而不是一片水域。

entries.definition: ocean plus -ic: relating to the ocean, or simply very large and open, as in oceanic distances.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -ic：与海洋有关的，或形容极其辽阔开阔的，如「远洋般的距离」。

entries.definition: ocean plus -graphy 'writing, describing': the scientific study of the sea, not the sea itself.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -graphy「书写、描述」：对海洋的科学研究，而不是海洋本身。

entries.definition: ocean plus front: land that faces the sea, so the compound names property rather than water.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 front：面朝大海的陆地，因此这个复合词指地产，而非水域。

entries.definition: a body of salt water smaller than an ocean and often partly enclosed by land; the everyday word for the water you can see from a shore.
entries.definitionCN: 比大洋小、常被陆地部分围住的咸水体；指岸边看得见的那片水的日常用词。

entries.definition: a plural used for a particular stretch of water, as in territorial waters; it is neutral in size and common in law and news.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指某一片特定水域，如领海；不限定规模，常见于法律与新闻。

entries.definition: an old poetic word for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main; it survives mostly in verse and historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指开阔大海的古雅诗歌用词，如「西班牙海」；如今多存于诗歌与历史写作。

entries.definition: the deep is a literary name for the sea that stresses its depth rather than its width; it fits images of sinking and hiding.
entries.definitionCN: the deep 是海洋的文学称呼，强调深度而非广度；适合「沉没、隐藏」一类意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek Okeanos was the river around the world, so the word began as one continuous ring of water.
normal.cn: 希腊语 Okeanos 是绕世界的大河，因此这个词最初就是一圈连着的水。

normal.en: The family runs ocean, oceanic, oceanography, oceanographer, oceanarium, oceanfront.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ocean、oceanic、oceanography、oceanographer、oceanarium、oceanfront。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: ocean floor, ocean basin, deep ocean, open ocean.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：海底、海盆、深海、开阔洋面。

normal.en: Geography names five: the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic oceans.
normal.cn: 地理学列出五个：太平洋、大西洋、印度洋、南大洋与北冰洋。

normal.en: The idiom an ocean of means a huge amount, as in an ocean of paperwork.
normal.cn: 短语 an ocean of 表示极多，如海量文书。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of water that cannot find a shore to belong to.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水找不到可以归属的岸。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the blue is not a colour but a distance you cannot cross.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，上面的蓝色不是颜色，而是一段跨不过去的距离。

abstract.en: Picture a voice heard across water, arriving in layers like waves.
abstract.cn: 想象隔着水传来的人声，一层一层像浪一样抵达。

examples.en: The ocean covers about seventy percent of the earth's surface.
examples.cn: 海洋覆盖了地球表面约七成。

examples.en: Scientists track how the ocean moves heat from the tropics poleward.
examples.cn: 科学家追踪海洋如何把热量从热带向极地输送。

examples.en: From the cliff we watched an ocean of cloud roll inland.
examples.cn: 从崖上望去，我们看着一片云海向内陆翻滚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，深海」——看到望不到边的水，先「哦」一声，再想到深海大洋 → 海洋、大量

root: 希腊 Okeanos「环绕世界的大河」（专名转普通名词）→ 拉丁 Oceanus → 古法语 occean → 英语 ocean；Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，或为前希腊语借词，构拟的印欧形式均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses radiate from one picture: a ring of salt water around the land, then the named parts, the water seen from a ship, the same boundlessness borrowed for quantity and feeling, and finally the water studied as a machine and claimed in law.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从同一个画面辐射出去：环绕陆地的咸水圈，然后是其中命名分区、船上所见的水面，同一份「无边」被借去指数量与情感，最后是当作机器研究的海洋与法律主张的海域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one continuous ring of salt water holding the land inside it, too wide to see across.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整圈连着的咸水把陆地围在里面，宽到看不见对岸。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BODY: the same water is first a place on the map and later a heat store studied by climate science.
branches.cn: 物理水体：同一片水先是地图上的一个地点，后来成为气候科学研究的储热系统。

branches.en: DIVIDED AND CLAIMED: geography cuts the whole into named oceans, and law marks where national claims stop.
branches.cn: 被划分与被主张：地理学把整体切成有名字的洋，法律标出国家主张止于何处。

branches.en: SEEN FROM A SHIP: from deck the water is a setting for travel, and as a modifier it labels the freight that crosses it.
branches.cn: 从船上看见：在甲板上水是旅行的场景，作定语时则标注穿越它的货运。

branches.en: BORROWED SCALE: the widest thing a speaker knows measures paperwork, sand and grass.
branches.cn: 借来的尺度：说话人知道的最宽之物，被用来度量文书、沙与草。

branches.en: INWARD WATER: grief and doubt become oceans because the person is inside them, not beside them.
branches.cn: 向内的水：悲伤与疑虑变成海洋，因为人是在其中，而不是在其旁。

intro.en: Ocean is a borrowed proper name that became a common noun; its family is built with Greek and Latin suffixes added to the same stem.
intro.cn: ocean 是一个转为普通名词的外来专名；它的词族都是在同一词干上加希腊语与拉丁语后缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: Latin Oceanus keeps both the name and the common noun, and oceanicus supplies the adjective pattern behind oceanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Oceanus 同时保留专名与普通名词用法，oceanicus 则提供了 oceanic 背后的形容词构词模式。

items.meaning: the stream believed to encircle the world
items.meaningCN: 古人想象中环绕世界的大河
items.example: Homer places Okeanos at the rim of the known world.
items.exampleCN: 荷马把 Okeanos 放在已知世界的边缘。

items.structure: Okeanos → Latin Oceanus → Old French occean
items.example: The ocean covers most of the planet.
items.exampleCN: 海洋覆盖了地球的大部分。

items.meaning: the scientific description of the sea
items.meaningCN: 对海洋的科学描述与研究
items.example: Oceanography combines chemistry, physics and biology.
items.exampleCN: 海洋学结合了化学、物理学与生物学。

items.meaning: a person who studies the sea
items.example: The oceanographer lowered a probe to the trench floor.
items.exampleCN: 海洋学家把探测器下放到海沟底部。

items.meaning: a large enclosure for living sea animals
items.meaningCN: 饲养活体海洋动物的大型场馆
items.example: The oceanarium rebuilt its reef tank.
items.exampleCN: 这座海洋馆重建了珊瑚礁展缸。

items.example: Oceanfront lots sold out within a week.

items.meaning: built for crossing the open sea
items.example: The yard launched an ocean-going tug.
items.exampleCN: 船厂下水了一艘远洋拖船。

items.meaning: the island region of the Pacific
items.exampleCN: 大洋洲包含成千上万座岛屿。

latinEntries.meaning: the great outer sea; also its divine name
latinEntries.meaningCN: 外围的大海；亦为海神之名

latinEntries.structure: oceanicus, oceanica, oceanicum (adj., first and second declension)
