senses.title: Not even: one left over after pairing
senses.titleCN: 奇数：两两配对后多出一个
senses.definition: of a number: having one left over when divided by two
senses.definitionCN: 指数目：被二除后余一
senses.example: Three is an odd number, so one chair is always empty.
senses.exampleCN: 三是奇数，所以总会空出一把椅子。
senses.why: Old Norse oddi meant 'a third or additional number', the unit beyond an even count. The oldest English sense is exactly this arithmetic one.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语 oddi 意为“第三个数、额外的数”，即成双之外多出的那一单位。英语最古老的义项正是这个算术义。

senses.title: Unpaired: the single one of a pair
senses.titleCN: 落单：一对里剩下的那只
senses.definition: of one of a pair: left without its partner and therefore unusable as a set
senses.definitionCN: 指一对中的一只：失去配对的另一只，因此无法成套使用
senses.example: One odd glove lay on the bench for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一只落单的手套在长椅上放了一周。
senses.why: The 'one over' count becomes a concrete object: if a pair is a set of two, the unit left over is the odd one, and the pair is broken.
senses.whyCN: “多出一个”的计数变成具体物件：一对是成双的集合，剩下的那一单位就是 odd，这一对也就散了。

senses.title: Occasional, not regular: odd jobs and odd moments
senses.titleCN: 零星的：不定时的零工与零碎时间
senses.definition: not forming part of a regular pattern; happening now and then
senses.definitionCN: 不构成规律的一部分；偶尔发生
senses.example: He takes odd jobs in the holidays to pay for books.
senses.exampleCN: 他假期打零工来买书。
senses.why: A job that does not belong to a regular set is the 'extra' unit again: isolated, unpaired, scattered through the week.
senses.whyCN: 不属于固定一套的活计又是那个“多余单位”：孤立、不成对、散落在一周里。

senses.title: Strange, peculiar
senses.definition: unusual or unexpected in a way that makes people uneasy or curious
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常或出乎意料，让人不安或好奇
senses.example: It was odd that the door stood unlocked all night.
senses.exampleCN: 门整夜没锁，这有点古怪。
senses.why: The 'strange' sense is recorded from the 1580s and grows from 'the odd one out': what does not fit the set draws attention and looks wrong.
senses.whyCN: “古怪”义自 16 世纪 80 年代有记录，从“落单的那一个”生长出来：不合群的东西招人注意，也显得不对劲。

senses.title: Slightly more than: forty-odd
senses.definition: used after a number to mean 'and a little more', as in forty-odd people
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字后表示“再多一点”，如 forty-odd people
senses.example: Thirty-odd people signed up for the night walk.
senses.exampleCN: 三十多个人报名参加了夜行。
senses.why: Here the leftover unit is attached to a round number: the count passes the round figure by an odd remainder, so the 'extra' becomes an approximation.
senses.whyCN: 这里多出的单位附在整数后面：数目超出整数一点点零头，于是“多余”变成约数。

senses.title: The odd one out: set apart from the group
senses.titleCN: 格格不入：被排除在群体之外
senses.definition: the person or thing that does not match the rest of a group
senses.definitionCN: 与群体其余成员不相配的人或物
senses.example: She was the odd one out in a family of musicians.
senses.exampleCN: 在一个音乐家家庭里，她是个例外。
senses.why: A set works by pairing; whoever cannot be paired is visibly separate. Being 'the odd one out' is the social version of the broken pair.
senses.whyCN: 一组东西靠配对成立；配不上对的那个就明显独立在外。“落单者”就是破碎配对的社会版本。

senses.title: Odds and ends: leftover scraps
senses.titleCN: 零碎杂物：用剩的边角料
senses.definition: in odds and ends, small useful items left over from larger things
senses.definitionCN: 用于 odds and ends，指大件用剩的小而有用之物
senses.example: The drawer was full of odds and ends: buttons, wire and old stamps.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉里塞满零碎东西：纽扣、铁丝和旧邮票。
senses.why: The plural odds means unequal remainders; combined with ends, it names the scraps that no longer belong to any complete set.
senses.whyCN: 复数 odds 指不相等的余数；与 ends 连用，就命名了那些不再属于任何完整套组的边角料。

senses.title: Odds: the chances of an outcome
senses.titleCN: 赔率与可能性：成败的差距
senses.definition: in the plural noun odds, the probability of one result rather than another, used in betting and in general prediction
senses.definitionCN: 复数名词 odds 指某一结果相对另一结果的可能性，用于赌博与一般预测
senses.example: The odds are against a rookie winning this tournament.
senses.exampleCN: 新手赢得这次比赛的可能性不大。
senses.why: Odds began as unequal numbers, a ratio that is not even. Betting turned that imbalance into a measure of chance: the odds are the unevenness of outcomes.
senses.whyCN: odds 起初指不相等的数，即不成偶的比例。博彩把这种不平衡变成机会的量度：赔率就是结果之间的不均等。

senses.title: Odd Fellow: a member of a friendly society
senses.titleCN: Odd Fellow：互助会会员（历史用法）
senses.definition: in the name Odd Fellows, a member of a fraternal benefit society that grew from local clubs in the late 18th century and was formally organised in 1813
senses.definitionCN: 在 Odd Fellows 这一名称中，指兄弟互助会的成员；该会由 18 世纪末的地方社团发展而来，1813 年正式组织
senses.example: He joined the Odd Fellows in 1813 and paid a small weekly sum for sickness cover.
senses.exampleCN: 他于 1813 年加入 Odd Fellows，每周缴一小笔钱以备生病。
senses.why: The society's name uses odd in the older sense of 'unusual companions': members were fellows of an odd sort, set apart from ordinary clubs. Odd Fellows is recorded as a local society late in the 18th century.
senses.whyCN: 这个会名用的是 odd 较旧的“奇怪的伙伴”义：成员是些“古怪的同伴”，与普通社团不同。Odd Fellows 作为地方社团记录于 18 世纪晚期。

intro.en: Odd is recorded around 1300 from Old Norse oddi 'a third or additional number'. The Norse word literally meant 'point of land, angle', and the step from 'point' to 'third number' is a development special to that language, so it is best marked as generally accepted.
intro.cn: odd 约于 1300 年从古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数、额外的数”进入英语。这个诺斯语词字面是“尖角、土地的一角”，而从“尖点”到“第三个数”这一步是该语言特有的发展，故宜标为“一般认为”。

items.en: Odde is recorded meaning 'constituting a unit in excess of an even number', the arithmetic sense that English still keeps.
items.cn: odde 记录为“构成超出偶数的一个单位”，这是英语至今保留的算术义。

items.en: From Old Norse oddi 'third or additional number'. The same word also meant 'point of land, angle'.
items.cn: 来自古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数、额外的数”，同一个词还表示“土地的一角、尖角”。

items.en: Odda-maðr meant 'the third man, the one who breaks a tie', and odda-tala meant 'odd number', showing the 'extra unit' idea already at work.
items.cn: odda-maðr 指“第三个人、打破平票的人”，odda-tala 指“奇数”，说明“多余单位”的观念已在运作。

items.en: Oddi is related through oddr 'point of a weapon' to Proto-Germanic *uzdaz 'pointed upward', which also gives Old English ord 'spear point, beginning', German Ort 'place', and Lithuanian usnis 'thistle'. The link from 'point' to 'third number' is not found outside Norse and is source uncertain.
items.cn: oddi 经 oddr“武器尖端”与原始日耳曼语 *uzdaz“朝上的尖”相关，后者也给出古英语 ord“矛尖、起点”、德语 Ort“地点”和立陶宛语 usnis“蓟”。从“尖点”到“第三个数”这一步在诺斯语之外未见，来源不确定。

items.en: The sense 'strange, peculiar' is recorded from the 1580s, growing out of the idea of the one left out of the set; a favourable sense 'singular, remarkable' appears around 1400.
items.cn: “古怪、奇特”义自 16 世纪 80 年代有记录，由“被排除在套组之外的那一个”发展而来；约 1400 年已有“非凡、稀有”的褒义。

items.en: Modern English adds fixed phrases: odd job (1728), odd lot (1897), and the Odd Fellows society, a local club in the late 18th century and formally organised in 1813.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了固定说法：odd job（1728）、odd lot（1897），以及 Odd Fellows 互助会——18 世纪晚期为地方社团，1813 年正式组织。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: a poem addressed to a person or thing. It sounds the same as odd but comes from Greek oide 'song'.
entries.definitionCN: 献给某人或某物的颂诗。它与 odd 同音，但词源是希腊语 oide“歌”。

entries.definition: the plural of odd in its 'unequal remainder' sense: chances, or odds and ends. It is not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: odd 在“不相等余数”义上的复数：可能性、赔率或零碎杂物。它不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: a strange person or thing. It is the noun built on odd with -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 怪人；怪事。它是由 odd 加 -ity 构成的名词。

entries.definition: unusual and hard to explain. It is the broad word, while odd often adds a touch of unease or mild humour.
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常且难以解释。它范围最广，odd 常多一层不安或轻微的调侃。

entries.definition: belonging to one person or thing in a way that stands out. It stresses distinctiveness, while odd stresses not fitting the set.
entries.definitionCN: 独特到显眼。它强调“专属、特别”，odd 强调“不合套组”。

entries.definition: unusual in a way that invites interest rather than unease. It is lighter and more neutral than odd.
entries.definitionCN: 奇特得引人好奇，而非令人不安。它比 odd 更轻、更中性。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Old Norse oddi 'third number', the odd one out, and the fixed phrases odd job, odds and ends and Odd Fellows.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数”、the odd one out，以及固定说法 odd job、odds and ends、Odd Fellows。

normal.en: Old Norse oddi meant the third or additional number, the unit that breaks a tie in a vote.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 oddi 指第三个数、额外的数，就是投票时打破平票的那一单位。

normal.en: A set works by pairs, so whatever cannot be paired is the odd one out.
normal.cn: 一套东西靠成对成立，配不上对的就是 the odd one out。

normal.en: Odd jobs are jobs that belong to no regular set; they are scattered and unpaired.
normal.cn: odd jobs 是不属于任何固定套组的活，零散而不成对。

normal.en: Odds and ends keeps the 'unequal remainder' idea: the scraps that no longer complete anything.
normal.cn: odds and ends 保留“不相等余数”的观念：再也凑不成完整东西的边角料。

normal.en: The arithmetic sense is the oldest: 1, 3, 5 are odd because one is always left over.
normal.cn: 算术义最古老：1、3、5 是奇数，因为每次都余下一个。

abstract.en: Picture three stones on a table: two can be paired, the third sits alone with a sharp corner showing.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上三块石头：两块能配上对，第三块孤零零待着，露出一个尖角。

abstract.en: The lone stone is arithmetic first, then a single glove, then a job that fits no schedule.
abstract.cn: 这块孤石先是算术，再是一只单手套，再是一份不合日程的零工。

abstract.en: When the lone stone is a person, the set's eyes turn on it, and 'left out' becomes 'strange'.
abstract.cn: 当孤石是一个人的时候，整套东西的目光都转向他，“落单”就变成了“古怪”。

examples.en: The street has odd numbers on one side and even numbers on the other.
examples.cn: 这条街一侧是奇数门牌，另一侧是偶数门牌。

examples.en: It seemed odd that such a careful man had left his bag on the train.
examples.cn: 这么细心的一个人竟把包落在火车上，显得很奇怪。

examples.en: She spent the afternoon sorting odds and ends in the bottom drawer.
examples.cn: 她花了一个下午整理最底层抽屉里的零碎东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥德」——奥德洗完衣服只剩一只袜子，又单又怪 → odd 单数的、落单的、古怪的

root: 源自约 1300 年的古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数、额外的数”，字面又指“土地的一角、尖角”，经 oddr“武器尖端”追到原始日耳曼语 *uzdaz“朝上的尖”；从“尖点”到“第三个数”这一步一般认为来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of odd all start from one picture: a unit that cannot be paired. That leftover then becomes an odd number, a single glove, a scattered job, a person set apart, a rough count, and finally the feeling of strangeness.
sensesIntro.cn: odd 的九个义项都从同一幅画出发：一个无法配对成双的单位。这个余数随后变成奇数、单只手套、零散活计、被排除在外的人、粗略的约数，最后变成“古怪”的感觉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one extra unit standing alone beside a matched pair.
core.cn: 核心意象：一对配好的东西旁边，多出一个独自站着的单位。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: the oldest branch, where one is always left over after pairing.
branches.cn: 数目：最古老的分支，两两配对后总会余下一。

branches.en: THE EXTRA UNIT: a single glove, a count a little past the round number, and the scraps that complete nothing.
branches.cn: 多出的单位：单只手套、略超整数的数目，以及凑不成任何东西的边角料。

branches.en: THE IRREGULAR: work and moments that belong to no fixed set and come only now and then.
branches.cn: 不规律：不属于固定套组、只是偶尔出现的工作与时刻。

branches.en: SET APART: the one a group cannot pair with, which draws attention, looks strange, and gives the Odd Fellows their name.
branches.cn: 被排除在外：群体配不上的那一个，它招来注意、显得古怪，也给 Odd Fellows 提供了名字。

branches.en: THE ODDs: unequal numbers turned into a measure of chance and betting.
branches.cn: 赔率：把不相等的数变成机会与赌博的量度。

intro.en: Odd is a bare Norse root with no living English prefix. English builds oddity with -ity and odds with the plural -s, and joins it into compounds such as oddball and odd-looking.
intro.cn: odd 是光秃的诺斯语词根，没有活的英语前缀。英语用 -ity 构成 oddity，用复数 -s 构成 odds，并把它并入 oddball、odd-looking 一类复合词。

latinIntro.en: Odd has no Latin source. Its recorded path is Old Norse oddi and, deeper, Proto-Germanic *uzdaz; the two entries below give those older forms rather than Latin words.
latinIntro.cn: odd 没有拉丁语来源。它的记录路径是古诺斯语 oddi，更深处是原始日耳曼语 *uzdaz；下面两条给出这些更早的形式，而不是拉丁词。

items.structure: odd (bare adjective from Old Norse oddi)
items.meaningCN: 奇数的；不成对的；零星的；古怪的

items.meaning: in a strange or unexpected way
items.meaningCN: 奇怪地；出乎意料地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 房间里安静得有些奇怪。

items.meaningCN: 奇怪；古怪（-ness 构成状态名词）
items.example: There was an oddness about the whole arrangement.
items.exampleCN: 整个安排透着一种古怪。

items.meaningCN: 怪人；怪事；古怪之处（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The museum is full of mechanical oddities.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆里满是奇巧的机械装置。

items.example: Her oddball uncle kept a boat in the garden.
items.exampleCN: 她那古怪的叔叔在花园里放了一条船。

items.meaning: a leftover piece; a miscellaneous item
items.meaningCN: 零头；残余物；零星物品（-ment 构成名词）
items.example: A box of oddments sat on the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 架子上放着一盒零碎东西。

items.meaningCN: 可能性；赔率；零碎杂物（复数形式）
items.example: The odds of rain tomorrow are high.
items.exampleCN: 明天下雨的可能性很大。

items.meaningCN: 样子古怪的（复合形容词）
items.example: An odd-looking parcel arrived by post.
items.exampleCN: 一个样子古怪的包裹寄到了。

latinEntries.meaning: a third or additional number; point of land, angle
latinEntries.meaningCN: 第三个数、额外的数；土地的一角、尖角（古诺斯语）

definition_zh: 奇怪地；古怪地；异常地；说来奇怪
definition_en: in a strange or unexpected way, to a surprising degree, and in the phrase oddly enough, used to introduce a fact that seems unlikely
core_image: 街角的路灯忽明忽暗，光晕一圈圈抖动着
scene: 雨夜的街角没有人，只有一盏老路灯在门边闪个不停，路人抬头看了一眼便加快脚步。The lamp above the door behaved oddly, flickering every few seconds.
sceneCN: 这里的 oddly 是「奇怪地、古怪地」（第 1 个义项：以反常的方式）；句意为门上方那盏灯表现得很古怪，每隔几秒就闪一下。图中可辨识物件：路灯、湿地面、门边光晕。

pos.zh: 奇怪地；古怪地；异常地

derivatives.zh: 由古诺尔斯语 oddi（尖角、三角形）进入英语，义为「奇怪的；单数的」
由 odd 加 -ness 构成，义为「古怪；奇特」
由 odd 加 -ity 构成，义为「怪事；怪人」

senses.title: In a strange or unusual way
senses.definition: in a way that strikes other people as strange, unexpected or hard to explain
senses.definitionCN: 以让别人觉得奇怪、出乎意料或难以解释的方式
senses.example: The machine started up, then stopped oddly after a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 机器启动了，一分钟后却古怪地停了下来。
senses.why: The adjective odd first named something unmatched or off to one side, so the adverb says an action sits apart from what anyone expects.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 odd 最初指「不成对、偏在一边」的东西，因此这个副词表示某个举动与人们预想的对不上。

senses.title: To a surprising degree
senses.definition: used before an adjective to say that the quality is stronger than one would expect
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，表示这种性质比人们预想的更强烈
senses.example: The street was oddly quiet for a Friday night.
senses.exampleCN: 对一个星期五的夜晚来说，这条街安静得出奇。
senses.why: What is unmatched also stands out from the group, and standing out easily turns into 'more than expected', so the adverb can simply intensify.
senses.whyCN: 不成对的东西也会从群体里凸显出来，而凸显很容易转成「超出预料」，于是这个副词也能起加强作用。

senses.title: Used to introduce a surprising fact
senses.definition: used in the phrase oddly enough to bring in a fact that seems strange but is true
senses.definitionCN: 用于 oddly enough 这一说法，引出一个显得奇怪却属实的情况
senses.example: Oddly enough, nobody in the family had ever seen the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 说来奇怪，这家人竟从没有谁见过海。
senses.why: A speaker marks a fact as odd before telling it, warning listeners that the next words will not fit their expectations.
senses.whyCN: 说话的人先把这个事实标为「古怪」，再讲出来，等于提醒听的人：接下来的话不合你的预期。

intro.en: Oddly is the adverb made from odd, and odd reached English from Old Norse rather than from Latin or French; the suffix -ly simply turns the adjective into a manner word.
intro.cn: oddly 是由 odd 构成的副词，而 odd 是从古诺尔斯语而不是拉丁语或法语进入英语的；后缀 -ly 只是把形容词变成方式副词。

items.en: Oddi named a point of land, a triangle or the third, unpaired item, and the word came south with Norse settlers.
items.cn: oddi 指一块尖角地、一个三角形，或第三个落单的东西，这个词随诺尔斯移民南传。

items.en: English borrowed the form as odd and used it first for a number that cannot be paired, such as three or five.
items.cn: 英语借入该形式作 odd，最初用来指三、五这样不能两两成对的数。

items.en: Being without a partner made the word a natural label for anything left over, extra or unlike its neighbours.
items.cn: 「没有同伴」这一情况使这个词自然用来指任何剩下的、多出来的或与左邻右舍不同的东西。

items.en: From 'unlike the others' came the modern sense of strange, unusual or slightly wrong, which the nineteenth century fixed in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 由「与别的不同」生出「奇怪、反常、略有毛病」的现代义，这一用法在十九世纪的日常口语中固定下来。

items.en: Modern English uses odd for unpaired numbers, for strange things, and in informal phrases like the odd one out; oddly carries all of this into adverb form.
items.cn: 现代英语用 odd 指单数、指古怪之物，也用于 the odd one out 这类口语说法；oddly 把这些意思带进副词形式。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family that grew from odd; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs for things done or felt in an unexpected way.
note.cn: 形近组收由 odd 生长出来的词族；近义组收其他表示「以出人意料的方式」的副词。

entries.definition: Not paired with another, or strange and unexpected.
entries.definitionCN: 不成对的，或奇怪的、出人意料的。

entries.definition: A strange thing, or a person who seems unusual.
entries.definitionCN: 古怪的事物，或显得与众不同的人。

entries.definition: The quality of being strange or unlike others.
entries.definitionCN: 古怪、与众不同的性质。

entries.definition: A person thought to be strange or eccentric.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为古怪、不合群的人。

entries.definition: In a way that is hard to explain or not familiar.
entries.definitionCN: 以难以解释或让人不熟悉的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that excites interest because it is unusual.
entries.definitionCN: 以因不寻常而引人好奇的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that belongs to one thing alone and is therefore odd.
entries.definitionCN: 以独特因而显得古怪的方式。

entries.definition: More than is common or expected.
entries.definitionCN: 比平常或预期更多、更强。

normalIntro.en: Oddly is odd with -ly on its back, and odd itself came in from Old Norse meaning the item left without a partner.
normalIntro.cn: oddly 是 odd 背上加了 -ly，而 odd 本身来自古诺尔斯语，指落单、没有配对的那一个。

normal.en: Oddly is simply odd plus -ly, the regular way English makes a manner adverb from an adjective.
normal.cn: oddly 就是 odd 加 -ly，是英语把形容词变成方式副词的常规做法。

normal.en: Odd first meant an unpaired number, which is why odd numbers and even numbers are still taught in pairs.
normal.cn: odd 最初指不成对的数，所以单数与偶数至今还是成对地教。

normal.en: From unpaired came the idea of unlike the rest, and from unlike the rest came the sense of strange.
normal.cn: 由「不成对」生出「与其余不同」，再由「不同」生出「奇怪」的意思。

normal.en: Oddly enough is a fixed opening: the speaker flags the surprise before delivering it.
normal.cn: oddly enough 是固定开场语：说话人先把意外标出来，再讲内容。

normal.en: Oddly quiet and oddly familiar put the adverb before an adjective to sharpen a quality, not to describe an action.
normal.cn: oddly quiet 与 oddly familiar 把副词放在形容词前，用来加强某种性质，而不是描述动作。

abstract.en: The word began with the one sock left over, which is why strangeness and loneliness sit so close in it.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于落单的那只袜子，所以「古怪」与「孤单」在它里面挨得那么近。

abstract.en: To say a thing is done oddly is to measure it against a pattern nobody wrote down.
abstract.cn: 说一件事做得古怪，就是拿它去量一个谁也没写下来的模式。

abstract.en: Oddly enough admits that the world can be true and unlikely at the same time.
abstract.cn: oddly enough 承认：世界可以同时是真的又是不大可能的。

examples.en: She smiled oddly and said nothing about the letter.
examples.cn: 她古怪地笑了笑，对那封信什么也没说。

examples.en: The room felt oddly cold in the middle of summer.
examples.cn: 盛夏里这间屋子却异常地冷。

examples.en: Oddly enough, the cheapest plan worked best.
examples.cn: 说来奇怪，最便宜的那个方案反而最管用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿得厉害」——饿得厉害了，看什么都觉得古怪；记住 oddly 是奇怪地。

root: 由 odd 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；odd 来自古诺尔斯语 oddi（尖角、三角形、落单的第三个），先指不成对的数，再指奇怪、反常。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the unpaired item standing apart from the rest; the adverb then covers odd behaviour, an odd degree of a quality, and the phrase that flags a surprise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是落单、与其余分开的那一个；副词由此覆盖古怪的举动、出奇的性质程度，以及用来标示意外的那一说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street lamp at the corner that keeps flickering, its halo trembling.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角的路灯忽明忽暗，光晕一圈圈抖动着。

branches.en: a lamp flickering above a wet doorway
branches.cn: 湿漉漉的门上方闪个不停的灯

branches.en: a street too silent for a Friday night
branches.cn: 星期五夜里静得过分的街道

branches.en: a family that never once saw the sea
branches.cn: 一家人竟谁也没见过海

branches.en: the same sense of something not fitting the scene
branches.cn: 同一种「与场景不相称」的感觉

branches.en: an adverb placed before an adjective to sharpen it
branches.cn: 放在形容词前、用来加强它的副词

intro.en: The word is an Old Norse adjective that English adopted, then fitted with the ordinary adverb ending -ly; the rest of its family grew by adding noun suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语采用的一个古诺尔斯语形容词，再加上常规的副词后缀 -ly；词族其余成员靠加名词后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for odd, which came into English from Old Norse and has no Latin ancestor behind it.
latinIntro.cn: odd 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它经古诺尔斯语进入英语，背后没有拉丁语祖先。

items.meaning: a point, a triangle, an unpaired third
items.meaningCN: 尖角；三角形；落单的第三个

definition_zh: 可能性；概率；赔率；不和；不利条件
definition_en: the chance that something will or will not happen, the figures that show this chance in betting, a state of disagreement, and the difficulties that work against success
core_image: 赛马场边的木牌上，一串数字跟着人群的喊声上下翻动
scene: 赛马场的围栏边挤满了人，看台上的示数牌随着下注一笔笔变动，有人低声算着自己那匹马的机会。The odds on the grey horse fell as the crowd put money down.
sceneCN: 这里的 odds 是「赔率」（第 2 个义项：博彩中表示机会大小的数字）；句意为随着人群下注，那匹灰马的赔率下降了。图中可辨识物件：围栏、示数牌、马匹。

pos.zh: 可能性；概率；赔率；不和；不利条件

derivatives.zh: odds 是 odd 的复数形式；odd 由古诺尔斯语 oddi 进入英语，义为「单数的；奇怪的」
由 odd 加 -ity 构成，义为「怪事；怪人」，与 odds 同出一源
由 odd 与 ball 复合而成，义为「古怪的人」

senses.title: The chance that something will happen
senses.definition: how likely it is that something will happen, often stated as a comparison between the chances of two outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能程度，常以两种结果的 chance 相互比较来表示
senses.example: The odds of finding a seat after noon are very low.
senses.exampleCN: 过了中午还想找到座位的可能性很低。
senses.why: The plural of odd once meant things that do not match, and unequal chances are exactly what probability compares, so odds became the name for the imbalance itself.
senses.whyCN: odd 的复数最初指彼此不相配的东西，而不相等的机会正是概率所要比较的，于是 odds 成了这种「不平衡」本身的名字。

senses.title: The figures offered in betting
senses.definition: the numbers set by a bookmaker to show how much a winning bet pays compared with the stake
senses.definitionCN: 博彩庄家设定的数字，表示中奖时能拿到多少钱与本金相比
senses.example: The odds on the outsider were fifty to one.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹冷门马的赔率是五十比一。
senses.why: Once people bet on unequal chances, the ratio of those chances becomes a price, and the word for imbalance turns into the figures on the board.
senses.whyCN: 人们一旦为不相等的机会下注，这些机会的比值就变成价格，表示「不平衡」的词也就变成了牌子上的数字。

senses.title: A state of disagreement
senses.definition: a condition in which two people, groups or accounts do not agree and are in conflict
senses.definitionCN: 两方人或两套说法互不同意、彼此冲突的状态
senses.example: The two managers have been at odds for months.
senses.exampleCN: 这两位经理已经不和好几个月了。
senses.why: Two things at odds are pulling in different directions, which is the same picture of things that fail to match, moved from numbers to people.
senses.whyCN: 处于 at odds 的两样东西朝不同方向使劲，仍是「对不上」这个画面，只是从数字挪到了人身上。

senses.title: Difficulties working against success
senses.definition: the unfavourable circumstances that make success less likely and must be overcome
senses.definitionCN: 使成功更困难、必须加以克服的不利情况
senses.example: She finished the race against all the odds.
senses.exampleCN: 她克服重重不利条件跑完了比赛。
senses.why: If odds measure how much the chances favour one side, then whatever stands on the weaker side is the odds against you, and the word comes to name hardship itself.
senses.whyCN: 如果 odds 衡量机会偏向哪一方，那么站在较弱一方的就是「对你不利的 odds」，这个词于是用来指艰难本身。

intro.en: Odds is the plural of odd, and odd came into English from Old Norse; the betting and disagreement senses grew out of the old idea of things that do not match.
intro.cn: odds 是 odd 的复数，而 odd 经古诺尔斯语进入英语；赔率与不和这两个义项，都是从「彼此不相配」这个旧意思里长出来的。

items.en: Oddi named a point, a triangle or an unpaired third item, and Norse settlers brought the word into English speech.
items.cn: oddi 指尖角、三角形或落单的第三个东西，诺尔斯移民把这个词带进了英语口语。

items.en: English used odd first for numbers that cannot be divided into two equal parts, then for anything left over or unlike the rest.
items.cn: 英语最初用 odd 指不能平分为两份的数，随后指任何剩下的或与其余不同的东西。

items.en: The plural odds named unequal things or a difference between sides, a sense recorded long before betting took it up.
items.cn: 复数形式 odds 指不相等的事物或两方的差额，这一义项在博彩采用它之前很久就有记录。

items.en: Bookmakers began to quote odds as the ratio between the money staked and the money paid, and the word settled into that everyday use.
items.cn: 庄家开始用 odds 报出下注金额与赔付金额之间的比值，这个词便在博彩的日常用法中固定下来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the plural form for chance, betting figures, disagreement in the phrase at odds, and the hardships summed up in against the odds.
items.cn: 现代英语保留复数形式，用来指机会、投注数字、at odds 一语中的不和，以及 against the odds 所概括的艰难。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family around odd; the near-meaning group collects words for chance, betting and open disagreement.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕 odd 的词族；近义组收表示机会、博彩以及公开分歧的词。

entries.definition: An unpaired number, or something strange and unexpected.
entries.definitionCN: 不成对的数，或奇怪、出人意料的事物。

entries.definition: A strange thing or a person who seems unusual.
entries.definitionCN: 古怪的事物，或显得不寻常的人。

entries.definition: A person whose behaviour strikes others as strange.
entries.definitionCN: 行为让人觉得古怪的人。

entries.definition: In a way that is strange or unexpected.
entries.definitionCN: 以奇怪或出人意料的方式。

entries.definition: The chance that something will happen.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能性。

entries.definition: A measured chance, often expressed as a figure between zero and one.
entries.definitionCN: 经过度量的可能性，常以零到一之间的数字表示。

entries.definition: The possibility that something may happen, especially when it is not certain.
entries.definitionCN: 某事可能发生的机会，尤指结果不确定时。

entries.definition: A situation in which people hold different views and do not agree.
entries.definitionCN: 人们各持不同看法、彼此不同意的情形。

normalIntro.en: Odds is odd made plural, and the plural carries the old idea of two sides that do not match, which is why chance, prices and quarrels all wear the same word.
normalIntro.cn: odds 是变成复数的 odd，而复数带着「两边对不上」的旧意思，所以机会、价码与口角都穿同一个词。

normal.en: Odd plus -s gives odds, and the plural is permanent: English keeps the s even when the meaning is a single chance.
normal.cn: odd 加 -s 得到 odds，这个复数是固定的：即使意思只是一次机会，英语也保留那个 s。

normal.en: Odd first named what cannot be paired, and odds names two sides whose chances are not level.
normal.cn: odd 最初指无法配对的东西，而 odds 指两边机会并不持平。

normal.en: At odds with someone keeps the picture of two sides pulling apart rather than matching.
normal.cn: at odds with 某人，保留了「两边分开使劲、并不吻合」的画面。

normal.en: Against the odds puts a person on the weaker side of those unequal chances, so the phrase means hardship.
normal.cn: against the odds 把人放到不相等机会中较弱的一边，因此这个说法意味着艰难。

normal.en: The phrase odds and ends survives as 'small leftovers', because odds once meant the extra, unmatched pieces.
normal.cn: odds and ends 作为「零碎杂物」保留下来，因为 odds 曾指多出来、配不上对的那几件。

abstract.en: Odds is the arithmetic of hope: it turns a feeling about the future into something that can be quoted and wagered.
abstract.cn: odds 是希望算术化：它把对未来的感觉变成可以报价、可以下注的东西。

abstract.en: That odds can mean both a probability and a quarrel suggests that disagreement is simply two chances pulling apart.
abstract.cn: odds 既能指概率又能指争吵，说明分歧不过是两个机会在朝两边分开。

abstract.en: To act against the odds is to bet on oneself when the numbers say otherwise.
abstract.cn: 顶着 odds 行事，就是在数字说「不」的时候把赌注押在自己身上。

examples.en: The odds of a late frost this month are quite low.
examples.cn: 这个月出现晚霜的可能性相当低。

examples.en: The bookmaker raised the odds just before the final.
examples.cn: 庄家在决赛前刚刚提高了赔率。

examples.en: He and his old partner have been at odds since the sale.
examples.cn: 自从那次出售之后，他和老搭档就一直不和。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「熬的」——机会是熬出来的，赔率也跟着数字走；记住 odds 是可能性与赔率。

root: odd（古诺尔斯语 oddi：尖角、落单的第三个）的复数形式；由「不相配、不相等」引申为可能性、赔率、不和与不利条件。

sensesIntro.en: The core is two sides that do not match; from that imbalance come the measured chance, the price quoted in betting, quarrels between people and the hardship of the weaker side.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两边对不上；由这种不平衡分出被量化的机会、博彩报出的价码、人之间的口角，以及较弱一方所承受的艰难。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scoreboard beside the racecourse where figures flip with every bet placed.
core.cn: 核心意象：赛马场边的示数牌，数字随每一笔下注上下翻动。

branches.en: a person weighing the chance of a seat after noon
branches.cn: 一个人估量下午还能不能找到座位

branches.en: figures on a board rising and falling with the money
branches.cn: 牌子上的数字随钱上下变动

branches.en: two managers refusing to sit at the same table
branches.cn: 两位经理拒绝同席

branches.en: a runner finishing after everyone had given up
branches.cn: 众人都放弃后仍跑完全程的人

branches.en: the same unequal balance seen in sums and in struggle
branches.cn: 数字与挣扎中同一种不平等的衡量

intro.en: The word is a plural noun with a visible adjective behind it, so its parts are odd, the plural ending and the phrases that carry the old idea of uneven sides.
intro.cn: 这个词是复数名词，背后有一个看得见的形容词，所以它的构件是 odd、复数词尾，以及承载「两边不齐」旧意思的若干说法。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for odd or odds, both of which reached English from Old Norse and stand outside the Latin family.
latinIntro.cn: odd 与 odds 都没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，二者都从古诺尔斯语进入英语，属于拉丁词族之外。

items.meaning: a point, a triangle, an unpaired third
items.meaningCN: 尖角；三角形；落单的第三个

items.meaning: to risk money on an outcome

definition_zh: ……的（所属）；来自；由……构成；关于；……的量
definition_en: a preposition marking possession or belonging, the source someone or something comes from, the material a thing is made from, the subject a statement is about, and the amount contained in a measure
core_image: 一只白瓷杯里盛着热茶，杯沿上绕着一缕白气
scene: 午后的厨房很安静，炉上的水刚停，桌上摆着一只白瓷杯和几片切好的柠檬。She poured a cup of tea and left it to cool by the window.
sceneCN: 这里的 of 是「……的量」（第 5 个义项：表示容器或单位所含的数量）；句意为她倒了一杯茶，放在窗边晾着。图中可辨识物件：白瓷杯、茶、柠檬片。

pos.zh: ……的；来自；由……构成；关于；……的量

derivatives.zh: 与 of 同源，来自古英语 æf 的强调形式，义为「离开；断开」
由 of 弱化而来的构词成分，见于 offshoot 等词，表示「离开、分出」
由 there 与 of 复合而成，义为「由此；关于那一点」

senses.title: Belonging to or connected with
senses.definition: used between two nouns to show that the second belongs to, is part of, or is connected with the first
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个名词之间，表示后者属于、构成或关联于前者
senses.example: The roof of the old house leaked in the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老房子的屋顶在暴风雨中漏了。
senses.why: Old English used the genitive ending on nouns for possession, and of, meaning 'from', gradually took over that work as endings wore away.
senses.whyCN: 古英语靠名词上的属格词尾表示所属，随着词尾逐渐磨损，意为「从……而来」的 of 慢慢接过了这项职能。

senses.title: Coming from a particular source
senses.definition: used after a noun to name the place, person or group that something comes from
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词后，指出某物来自的地方、人或群体
senses.example: She is a teacher of mathematics from a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位来自小镇的数学老师。
senses.why: The earliest sense of the word was 'away from', so naming where something starts out is one of its oldest jobs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的意思是「离开、从……而来」，所以指出某物的来处是它最古老的职能之一。

senses.title: Made or consisting of a material
senses.definition: used to name the substance a thing is made from or the parts that make it up
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出某物由什么材料制成，或由哪些部分构成
senses.example: The frame is made of bamboo and the seat of woven grass.
senses.exampleCN: 框架由竹子制成，座面则由编草做成。
senses.why: Once of marks where a thing comes from, it can also mark what it was built out of, since material is a kind of origin.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 of 标出某物的来处，它也能标出某物由什么造成，因为材料也是一种来源。

senses.title: About or concerning
senses.definition: used after certain verbs and nouns to introduce the subject that is being thought, spoken or written about
senses.definitionCN: 用在某些动词和名词后，引出被思考、谈论或书写的主题
senses.example: He told us a long story of the sea and its storms.
senses.exampleCN: 他给我们讲了一个关于大海和风暴的长故事。
senses.why: To speak of something is to start from it and move outward in words, so the preposition of source became the marker of a topic.
senses.whyCN: 说到某事物，就是以它为起点用话语向外展开，于是这个表示来源的介词也成了话题的标记。

senses.title: Showing the amount contained in a measure
senses.definition: used between a quantity word or container and the thing it measures, as in a cup of tea or a piece of paper
senses.definitionCN: 用在数量词或容器与它所量的东西之间，如 a cup of tea 或 a piece of paper
senses.example: He asked for a glass of water and a slice of bread.
senses.exampleCN: 他要了一杯水和一片面包。
senses.why: A measure is hollow until something fills it, so of joins the container to its contents and turns two words into one quantity.
senses.whyCN: 度量本身是空的，直到有东西把它填满，于是 of 把容器和内容连起来，让两个词合成一个数量。

intro.en: Of is one of the oldest English words, an unstressed form of a Germanic word meaning 'away from', and its modern uses grew as English lost the noun endings that once marked possession.
intro.cn: of 是英语最古老的词之一，是日耳曼语中表示「离开、从……而来」的词的非重读形式；随着英语丢掉曾经标示所属的名词词尾，它的现代用法才逐渐长成。

items.en: Scholars generally reconstruct a form meaning 'off, away from' behind this family, and the same source is thought to lie behind Greek apo and Latin ab.
items.cn: 学者一般认为这一族词背后有一个表示「离开、从……而来」的形式，并认为希腊语 apo 与拉丁语 ab 也出自同一来源。

items.en: The Germanic form carried the sense of moving away or departing, and it worked as an unstressed preposition rather than a stressed adverb.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式带着「离开、出发」的意思，且多作非重读介词，而不是重读副词。

items.en: Old English had æf, meaning away or from, alongside of as its weaker, unstressed form in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 古英语有 æf，意为「离开、从」，而 of 是它在日常口语中较弱、非重读的形式。

items.en: Middle English let of take over the possessive work of fading noun endings, so phrases like the roof of the house replaced older inflected forms.
items.cn: 中古英语让 of 接手逐渐消失的名词词尾的所属职能，于是 the roof of the house 这类说法取代了更早的屈折形式。

items.en: Modern English keeps of for possession, source, material, topic and quantity, while its stressed twin off survives as a separate word for departure.
items.cn: 现代英语让 of 承担所属、来源、材料、话题与数量，而它重读的双胞胎 off 作为表示「离开」的独立词留存下来。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words whose spelling or history stands close to of; the near-meaning group collects prepositions and phrases that express possession or origin.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或来历与 of 相近的词；近义组收表示所属或来源的介词与说法。

entries.definition: Away from a place, or not switched on; the stressed twin of of.
entries.definitionCN: 离开某处，或未接通电源；of 的重读双胞胎。

entries.definition: To present something for someone to accept; the spelling is close but the source is Latin offerre, so it is not related to of.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物呈上供人接受；只是拼写相近，词源不同，它来自拉丁语 offerre。

entries.definition: An old poetic shortening of often, meaning many times; it is only spelling that resembles of, the source is separate.
entries.definitionCN: often 的古老诗歌缩略形式，意为「多次」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Of that or of it, a formal word built by joining there and of.
entries.definitionCN: 关于那一点或它的，由 there 与 of 合成的正式用语。

entries.definition: A preposition marking the starting point or source of something.
entries.definitionCN: 标示某物起点或来源的介词。

entries.definition: A phrase saying that something is owned by or part of another.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某物归另一物所有或属于它的说法。

entries.definition: A preposition naming the subject of speech, thought or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 引出谈话、思考或写作主题的介词。

entries.definition: A phrase saying what substance something is produced out of.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某物由何种材料制成的说法。

normalIntro.en: Of is a tiny word doing several large jobs at once, and every hook follows the one old idea of starting out from something.
normalIntro.cn: of 是个小词，却同时干着好几件大事，而每条记忆钩子都顺着「从某处出发」这个古老想法。

normal.en: Old English æf meant away or from, and of was simply its light, unstressed form in quick speech.
normal.cn: 古英语 æf 意为「离开、从」，of 只是它在快语速中轻读的形式。

normal.en: Off is the same word under stress, which is why a shop can be off a street and a lid can come off a box.
normal.cn: off 是同一个词的重读形式，所以一家店可以在街道拐出去的位置，盖子也能从盒子上取下来。

normal.en: English once put endings on nouns for possession; as those endings disappeared, of stepped in, giving the roof of the house.
normal.cn: 英语曾在名词上加词尾表示所属；这些词尾消失后，of 补了进来，于是有了 the roof of the house。

normal.en: A cup of tea joins container and contents, so the preposition turns two nouns into one measured amount.
normal.cn: a cup of tea 把容器与内容连在一起，这个介词就把两个名词合成一个被量出的数量。

normal.en: Of course, of mine and think of each freeze a different piece of grammar into a phrase worth learning whole.
normal.cn: of course、of mine 与 think of 各自把一处不同的语法冻成了值得整块记住的说法。

abstract.en: Of is the word English uses when one thing has to be anchored to another, whether by owner, origin, stuff or subject.
abstract.cn: 当一样东西必须拴到另一样上时，英语就动用 of，无论靠的是主人、来处、材料还是话题。

abstract.en: Its history shows a language quietly replacing its own grammar with a small preposition.
abstract.cn: 它的历史显示：一门语言悄悄用一个小介词替换掉了自己原有的语法。

abstract.en: A cup of tea is two nouns and a hinge, which is all most possession really is.
abstract.cn: a cup of tea 是两个名词加一个铰链，而多数「所属」其实也不过如此。

examples.en: The handle of the door came loose during the winter.
examples.cn: 门把手在冬天松动脱落了。

examples.en: She is a friend of my sister and lives in the same building.
examples.cn: 她是我姐姐的朋友，住在这栋楼里。

examples.en: They drank a pot of tea and talked until midnight.
examples.cn: 他们喝了一壶茶，一直聊到半夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶夫」——偶然遇到的丈夫，说起「什么东西的」；记住 of 是「……的」。

senses.title: An illegal act; a crime
senses.definition: an act that is forbidden by law and can be punished by the state
senses.definitionCN: 法律禁止、可由国家加以惩罚的行为
senses.example: Driving without insurance is a serious offence.
senses.exampleCN: 无保险驾驶是一项严重违法行为。
senses.why: Latin offensa named a striking against something, and English narrowed that image to a wrong the law can punish.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 offensa 本指「撞上、触犯」，英语把这幅画面收窄为法律可以惩罚的过错。

senses.title: The act of upsetting someone
senses.definition: the feeling of being insulted, or the act of saying something that hurts someone
senses.definitionCN: 被人侮辱的感受，或说出使人受伤的话这一行为
senses.example: She took offence at his remark about her accent.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿她的口音开玩笑，她为此生了气。
senses.why: If a word can name a blow, it can also name the sting left by a careless remark, so the same noun covers social injury.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指一次打击，也就能指一句无心之言留下的刺痛，所以同一个名词也覆盖人情上的伤害。

senses.title: A breaking of the rules in sport
senses.definition: an action that breaks the rules of a game and is punished by the referee
senses.definitionCN: 违反比赛规则、由裁判加以处罚的动作
senses.example: The referee stopped play for a handball offence.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判因手球犯规中止了比赛。
senses.why: A game is a small legal system, so the legal sense of a punishable wrong transfers easily to the pitch.
senses.whyCN: 球赛是一套小型的规则体系，法律上「可受罚的过错」这层意思很自然就挪到了球场上。

senses.title: The attacking side or attacking play
senses.definition: the part of a team or of a game that attacks, as opposed to defence
senses.definitionCN: 一支球队或一场比赛中负责进攻的一方，与防守相对
senses.example: Their offence moved the ball quickly up the left side.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的进攻沿着左路快速推进。
senses.why: The word already carries the image of moving against something, so a team pushing forward is called the offence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就带着「朝着某物撞过去」的画面，所以向前推进的一方被称作进攻。

intro.en: Offence is the noun of a Latin verb for striking against, and it reached English through French with both a legal and a personal sense.
intro.cn: offence 是拉丁语中「撞上去」这一动词的名词形式，经法语进入英语，同时带来法律与人情两层含义。

items.en: The verb offendere was built from ob-, meaning against, and fendere, meaning to strike, so it pictured a blow aimed at something.
items.cn: 动词 offendere 由表示「对着、朝向」的 ob- 与表示「打击」的 fendere 构成，画面是朝着某物打过去的一击。

items.en: The noun offensa grew from that verb and meant a striking against, an obstacle, and a wrong that had been committed.
items.cn: 名词 offensa 从这一动词长出，指撞上、障碍，以及已经犯下的过错。

items.en: Old French passed the noun on as offense, keeping both the legal sense of a wrong and the sense of being insulted.
items.cn: 古法语把这一名词写作 offense 传入，既保留「过错」的法律义，也保留「被冒犯」的感受义。

items.en: Middle English offence covered crimes, sins and personal slights, and the spelling settled with a c before i.
items.cn: 中古英语的 offence 同时指罪行、罪过和人情上的冒犯，拼写在 i 之前逐渐固定为 c。

items.en: British English keeps offence while American English writes offense, the form closer to Latin offensa.
items.cn: 现代英式英语保留 offence，美式英语写作 offense，后者更接近拉丁语 offensa 的拼法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the verb, the American spelling and the word family built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers legal and social words for wrongdoing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的动词、美式拼写与词族；近义组收法律与人情两方面表示过错的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin stem for striking, and its family keeps returning to blows that land on people, rules and laws.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「打击」的拉丁词干上，同族词反复回到落在人、规则与法律上的那一击。

normal.en: Latin fendere means to strike, and ob- means against, so offence is literally a blow aimed at someone.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 fendere 意为打击，ob- 意为对着，所以 offence 字面上就是朝人打出的一击。

normal.en: Offence and offend are one family: the verb is the blow, the noun is the blow and the wrong it leaves.
normal.cn: offence 与 offend 同属一族：动词是那一击，名词既是这一击，也是它留下的过错。

normal.en: British spelling keeps the c, American spelling writes offense, which is closer to Latin offensa.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留 c，美式写作 offense，更接近拉丁语 offensa。

normal.en: Take offence means to treat another person's words as a blow aimed at you.
normal.cn: take offence 意为「见怪」，就是把他人的话当成朝自己打来的一击。

normal.en: Criminal offence stretches the same word from a rude remark all the way to a punishable crime.

abstract.en: The same noun covers a rude word and a crime, which shows that harm is only a matter of degree.

senses.title: To commit a crime or a wrong
senses.definition: to commit a crime or do something morally wrong
senses.definitionCN: 犯下罪行，或做出道德上错误的事
senses.example: He offended repeatedly before he was finally caught.
senses.exampleCN: 他屡次作案，最终才被抓。
senses.why: Offendere also meant to stumble or to transgress, and English kept that sense for breaking a law or a moral code.
senses.whyCN: offendere 也有「失足、越界」的意思，英语保留了这层，用来指触犯法律或道德规范。

senses.title: To break a rule or principle
senses.definition: to go against a rule, a principle or a standard
senses.definitionCN: 违背某条规则、原则或标准
senses.example: The new policy offends against the principle of equal pay.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策违反了同工同酬的原则。
senses.why: With against, the verb points the blow at an abstract standard rather than a person, so the insult turns into a violation.
senses.whyCN: 接上 against 时，这一击指向的不再是人，而是一条抽象标准，于是「冒犯」转为「违反」。

senses.title: To be unpleasant to the senses
senses.definition: to be offensive to the eye, the ear or the nose
senses.definitionCN: 使眼睛、耳朵或鼻子感到不适
senses.example: The bright green paint offends the eye in that quiet room.
senses.exampleCN: 在那间素净的屋子里，那面亮绿色的墙看着很扎眼。
senses.why: Since a blow can land on the body, the same verb can describe what jars the senses, which is the last step from people to eyes and noses.
senses.whyCN: 既然一击能落在人身上，同一个动词也能形容刺到感官的东西，这就是从人走到眼睛与鼻子的最后一步。

intro.en: Offend is a Latin verb for striking against that came through French, and its sense moved from stumbling and sinning to hurting feelings.
intro.cn: offend 是拉丁语中表示「撞上去」的动词，经法语进入英语，词义从失足、犯罪一路走到伤害感情。

items.en: Offendere joined ob-, meaning against, with fendere, meaning to strike, so its first picture was a blow aimed at something.
items.cn: offendere 把表示「对着」的 ob- 与表示「打击」的 fendere 合在一起，最初的画面是朝着某物打出一击。

items.en: In Latin the verb also meant to stumble against an obstacle and to transgress, which prepared the later moral senses.
items.cn: 在拉丁语中，这个动词还表示撞上障碍、失足，以及越界，这为后来的道德义埋下了伏笔。

items.en: Old French offendre meant to wrong or to sin, and it supplied English with the verb in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语 offendre 意为冒犯或犯罪，中世纪时把这个动词送进了英语。

items.en: Middle English offenden first meant to sin or to transgress, and only later came to mean to displease a person.
items.cn: 中古英语的 offenden 最初指犯罪、越界，后来才引申为使人不快。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the legal sense of breaking a rule and the everyday sense of hurting someone's feelings.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留「违反规则」的法律义与「伤害感情」的日常义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and adjectives of the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for hurting feelings and breaking rules.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词族的名词与形容词；近义组收表示伤人感情与违反规则的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a crime or for the act of upsetting someone.
entries.definitionCN: 表示罪行或冒犯行为的英式名词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the noun related to offend.
entries.definitionCN: 与 offend 相关的名词的美式拼写。

entries.definition: An adjective and noun from the same stem, meaning insulting or attacking.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的形容词兼名词，义为冒犯的或进攻的。

entries.definition: A person who offends or breaks the law.
entries.definitionCN: 冒犯他人或违反法律的人。

entries.definition: To say something rude that hurts or humiliates someone.
entries.definitionCN: 说出粗鲁的话，伤害或羞辱他人。

entries.definition: To make someone feel unhappy, worried or annoyed.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人感到不快、担心或恼火。

entries.definition: To make someone feel annoyed or not satisfied.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人感到不快或不满意。

entries.definition: To break a law, a rule or an agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 违反法律、规则或约定。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of striking that turned into a family of nouns and adjectives about wrongdoing and wounded feelings.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示打击的动词，后来长成一族指过错与伤人感情的名词与形容词。

normal.en: Ob- plus fendere gives a blow aimed at someone, and that is the physical core of offend.
normal.cn: ob- 加 fendere 就是朝人打出的一击，这就是 offend 的身体性内核。

normal.en: Offend against is the pattern for breaking a law or a principle, not for hurting a person.
normal.cn: offend against 是违反法律或原则的固定搭配，而不是指伤害某个人。

normal.en: Offender adds -er to the verb: the person who lands the blow or commits the crime.
normal.cn: offender 在动词后加 -er，就是打出这一击、犯下罪行的那个人。

normal.en: Be offended by marks the receiver of the blow, the person whose feelings were hurt.
normal.cn: be offended by 标出的是承受一击的一方，也就是感情受伤的人。

normal.en: Offend the eye shows that the verb can strike senses as well as feelings.
normal.cn: offend the eye 说明这个动词不只打击感情，也能打击感官。

abstract.en: Picture a small stone thrown in conversation: it leaves no mark on the skin, but offend names the bruise underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象谈话中扔出的一颗小石子：皮肤上没有痕迹，而 offend 就是底下那块淤青的名字。

abstract.en: A step over a rule touches the law first and someone's feelings second, and one verb covers both.
abstract.cn: 越过规则的那一步，先触到法律，再触到别人的感受，同一个动词把两者都收下了。

abstract.en: Offence is often unintended, yet it still lands on the other person; that gap is what the word keeps alive.
abstract.cn: 冒犯常常不是本意，却仍然落在对方身上；这道落差正是这个词一直保留的东西。

examples.en: His joke offended several guests at the party.
examples.cn: 他那个玩笑得罪了聚会上的好几位客人。

examples.en: The new policy offends against the principle of equal pay.
examples.cn: 新政策违反了同工同酬的原则。

examples.en: Loud colours offend the eye in such a quiet room.
examples.cn: 在这样素净的房间里，刺眼的颜色看着很不舒服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，犯的」——哦，是他犯的；offend 既是冒犯别人，也是犯了事。

root: 拉丁语 offendere（撞上、触犯）由 ob-（对着）加 fendere（打击）构成，经古法语 offendre 进入英语；同族词有 offence、offensive、offender。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a blow aimed at someone; the senses divide into wounded feelings, broken law, broken rule and jarred senses.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「朝人打出的一击」；义项分为受伤的感情、触犯的法律、违反的规则与受刺激的感官。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching out without a fist, still bumping into another person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只没有握成拳的手伸出去，还是撞到了别人。

branches.en: a joke that makes a face at the table go cold
branches.cn: 一句玩笑让桌边一张脸冷下来

branches.en: a man standing in the dock after repeated thefts
branches.cn: 屡次行窃的人站在被告席上

branches.en: a new clause that clashes with an old principle
branches.cn: 新条款与旧原则相抵触

branches.en: harsh light and a sharp smell that make people turn away
branches.cn: 强光与刺鼻气味让人别过脸

branches.en: the same force that wounds a person can also wound an eye
branches.cn: 伤人的那股力，也能伤到一双眼睛

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin prefix of direction, a root for striking, the Latin verb built from them, and two English suffixes for the person and the resulting quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示方向的拉丁前缀、表示打击的词根、由二者构成的拉丁动词，以及分别指「人」和「由此生出的性质」的两个英语后缀支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

senses.title: A punishable illegal act
senses.definition: an act that breaks the law and can be punished
senses.definitionCN: 违反法律并可受处罚的行为
senses.example: Parking without a permit is a minor offense in this district.
senses.exampleCN: 在本区无证停车属于轻微违法。
senses.why: Latin offensa meant 'a striking against': an offence is conduct that strikes against a rule.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 offensa 意为「撞上、触犯」：违法行为就是撞上规则的行为。

senses.title: An act of insult
senses.definition: something said or done that hurts or angers another person
senses.definitionCN: 伤害或激怒他人的言行
senses.example: He took her remark as an offense and left the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他把她那句话当作冒犯，离开了餐桌。
senses.why: The same image of striking against serves here: the blow lands on a person rather than on a rule.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「撞上」的形象在此落在人身上，而不是落在规则上。

senses.title: The attacking side in sport
senses.definition: the team or players whose job is to score
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中负责得分的一方或球员
senses.example: Their offense scored on the first possession.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的进攻组在第一次进攻中就得分了。
senses.why: Military attack language moved into sport, where the offense is the side that strikes.
senses.whyCN: 军事攻击的说法进入体育，那里「进攻」指负责击打的一方。

senses.title: A military attack
senses.definition: a planned attack by armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 武装力量有计划的攻击
senses.example: The offense began at dawn along the eastern ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 攻势在黎明沿东侧山脊开始。
senses.why: The military sense keeps the original image of a blow, aimed across a line at an enemy.
senses.whyCN: 军事义保留了「一击」的原初形象，越过界线打向敌方。

senses.title: Something repellent
senses.definition: a thing that disgusts or offends the senses
senses.definitionCN: 令感官或情感反感的事物
senses.example: The smell was an offense to everyone in the carriage.
senses.exampleCN: 那股气味让车厢里所有人都难受。
senses.why: The noun can name the source of the displeasure, not only the act that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能指引起不快的行为，也能指不快本身的来源。

senses.title: A moral or religious transgression
senses.definition: a wrong considered against a moral or religious standard
senses.definitionCN: 依道德或宗教标准认定的过错
senses.example: In the old rite, the offense required a public apology.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧礼仪中，这种过失需要公开道歉。
senses.why: A moral code can be struck against just as a statute can, so the religious sense needs no courtroom.
senses.whyCN: 道德准则也会被「撞上」，正如法条会被撞上，因此宗教义不需要法庭。

senses.title: The state of being offended
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase take offense: to feel insulted
senses.definitionCN: 在「感到受辱」这一固定说法中，指被冒犯的状态
senses.example: She took offense at the question and did not answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个问题感到被冒犯，没有回答。
senses.why: The noun names not only the blow but the state of the one who received it, hence the fixed phrase for feeling insulted.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词不只指那一击，也指受击者的状态，因此有了表示「感到受辱」的固定说法。

senses.title: An attacking formation
senses.definition: the organised pattern or plan a team uses to attack
senses.definitionCN: 球队用于进攻的组织方式或计划
senses.example: The coach rebuilt the offense around two fast wings.
senses.exampleCN: 教练围绕两名快翼重建了进攻体系。
senses.why: Strategy talk turns the attacking side into a system with a name.
senses.whyCN: 战术话语把进攻方变成一个有名目的体系。

intro.en: Offense comes through Old French offense from Latin offensa 'a striking against, an injury, displeasure', from offendere, built on ob- 'against' and fendere 'to strike'. It is recorded in English from the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: offense 经古法语 offense 来自拉丁 offensa「撞击、伤害、不快」，出自 offendere，由 ob-「对着」与 fendere「击打」构成，十四世纪起在英语中有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fendere meant 'to strike'; it also underlies defend, where de- adds the sense of striking away.
items.cn: fendere 意为「击打」；它也是 defend 的词根，那里 de- 增添「打回去」的意思。

items.en: Ob- 'against' plus fendere gave offendere 'to strike against, to attack, to displease'.
items.cn: ob-「对着」加 fendere 构成 offendere「撞上、攻击、使不快」。

items.en: The noun offensa named a blow, an injury and the displeasure that followed.
items.cn: 名词 offensa 指一次撞击、一处伤害，以及随之而来的不快。

items.en: Old French offense carried both the legal and the personal senses into English.
items.cn: 古法语 offense 把法律义与个人感受义一并带入英语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century offense named the attacking half of a team, borrowing the military image.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，offense 指球队的进攻一半，借用了军事意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin origin of fendere is unsettled, so any older root proposed for it is a reconstruction; the exact first English citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：fendere 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，凡为其提出的更古老词根都属于重构；英语最早书证的确切年代不确定。

note.en: Group one holds words from the fendere stock, where prefixes reverse the direction of the blow; group two holds words for a breach or an insult.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 fendere 词干的词，前缀改变击打的方向；第二组是表示违法或冒犯的词。

entries.definition: The verb 'to strike against': to hurt someone's feelings or to break a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 「撞上去」的动词：伤害他人感受或违反规则。

entries.definition: De- 'away' plus fendere: to strike the blow away, hence to protect.
entries.definitionCN: de-「离开」加 fendere：把击打挡开，因此指防御。

entries.definition: The party who defends in a case; the word comes from defending, not from offending.
entries.definitionCN: 案件中作辩护的一方；这个词来自「防御」而非「冒犯」。

entries.definition: The adjective of offense, used for insults, attacks and attacking play.
entries.definitionCN: offense 的形容词，用于侮辱、攻击与进攻打法。

entries.definition: Any punishable illegal act; an offense may be minor, regulatory or military.
entries.definitionCN: 任何可罚的违法行为；offense 可以是轻微、规章性或军事性的。

entries.definition: A breaking of a specific rule or right, often administrative.
entries.definitionCN: 违反某条具体规则或权利，常属行政性质。

entries.definition: A remark that belittles a person, with no legal or military sense.
entries.definitionCN: 贬低他人的话语，不含法律或军事含义。

entries.definition: Bad conduct judged morally, which may or may not be an offense in law.
entries.definitionCN: 从道德上评判的不良行为，未必构成法律上的违法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ob- 'against' plus fendere 'strike': a blow aimed at a rule or a person.
normal.cn: ob-「对着」加 fendere「击打」：朝规则或朝人打去的一击。

normal.en: The family runs offend, offense, offensive, offender, offended.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 offend、offense、offensive、offender 与 offended。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: criminal offense, take offense, no offense.
normal.cn: 固定搭配切分义项：刑事罪行、感到被冒犯、无意冒犯。

normal.en: American spelling offense, British spelling offence; both are the same word.
normal.cn: 美式拼作 offense，英式拼作 offence，是同一个词。

normal.en: Defend uses the same root with the opposite prefix: the blow is struck away.
normal.cn: defend 用同一词根加相反前缀：把击打挡开。

abstract.en: Picture a hand striking a rulebook and then striking a person's pride.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手先打在规则手册上，又打在人的自尊上。

abstract.en: Picture a field split in two, one half pushing forward and one half holding.
abstract.cn: 想象球场分成两半，一半向前推，一半守住。

abstract.en: Picture a smell that enters a closed carriage and offends everyone in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一股气味进入密闭车厢，冒犯了里面所有人。

examples.en: The regulations list each offense and the fine attached to it.
examples.cn: 规章列出了每一项违法行为及对应的罚款。

examples.en: He apologised at once, saying he had meant no offense.
examples.cn: 他立刻道歉，说自己并无冒犯之意。

examples.en: The team's offense controlled the ball for most of the second half.
examples.cn: 该队的进攻组在下半场大部分时间控制着球。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「of（对着）+ fense（打）」——对着规则或人打过去：违法、冒犯、进攻

root: 拉丁 offensa「撞击、伤害、不快」= ob-（对着）+ fendere（击打）的过去分词 offensus；fendere 更深来源不确定。英语经古法语 offense 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one blow: it lands on a rule and becomes an offence, on a person and becomes an insult, then on a scoreboard, a battlefield, the senses, a moral code, one's own pride and finally a plan for attacking.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一击：打在规则上成为违法，打在个人身上成为冒犯，再打向记分牌、战场、感官、道德准则、自己的自尊，最后成为一种进攻方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ticket pushed across a table, with the other person's brow already lowering.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张罚单被推到桌子对面，对面的人已经皱起了眉。

branches.en: THE BLOW ON A RULE: conduct strikes a statute and becomes punishable.
branches.cn: 打在规则上：行为撞上法条，因而可受处罚。

branches.en: THE BLOW ON A PERSON: the same strike lands on feelings and becomes insult.
branches.cn: 打在个人身上：同一击落在情感上，成为冒犯。

branches.en: THE ORGANISED BLOW: a team and an army both keep a side whose job is to strike.
branches.cn: 有组织的一击：球队与军队都保留负责击打的一方。

branches.en: THE SOURCE AND THE SIN: a smell can repel the senses, and a moral code can name a transgression.
branches.cn: 来源与罪过：气味能令感官反感，道德准则也能指认过失。

branches.en: ONE'S OWN STATE AND THE PLAN: a person takes offence, and a coach designs an offence.
branches.cn: 自身状态与方案：个人会感到被冒犯，教练则设计进攻方案。

intro.en: Offense is a Latin noun whose prefix and root reverse direction to build defend as well.
intro.cn: offense 是一个拉丁名词，其前缀与词根换个方向也构成 defend。

latinIntro.en: Latin fendere 'to strike' gives offend, offense and defensive words; ob- aims the blow forward, de- strikes it away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fendere「击打」衍生 offend、offense 与一批防御类词；ob- 把击打朝前送去，de- 则把它格开。

items.example: The root carries the physical blow.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着实在的一击。
这个玩笑冒犯了两名听众。

items.meaning: a blow, an injury, a breach
items.example: The offense carried a small fine.
items.exampleCN: 这项违法行为附带小额罚款。

items.meaning: a person who breaks the law

definition_zh: 冒犯的；无礼的；令人反感的；进攻的；攻势
definition_en: causing someone to feel insulted or upset; extremely unpleasant; used for or taking the attack; as a noun, a planned military attack
core_image: 一句话和一支军队都朝着同一个方向推出去
scene: 看台上有人拉起一条嘲弄对方球队的横幅，周围的笑声很快变成了争吵。The referee warned that the banner was offensive and had to be removed.
sceneCN: 这里 offensive 是「冒犯的、无礼的」（第 1 个义项：使人感到被冒犯）；句意是裁判警告那条横幅带有冒犯意味，必须撤下。画面里有看台、横幅和争执的观众。

pos.zh: 冒犯的；无礼的；令人反感的；进攻的
攻势；进攻

derivatives.zh: 由 offensive 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「冒犯地；进攻性地」
由 offensive 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「冒犯性；令人反感的程度」
由同一拉丁词干 offensa 构成，义为「罪行；冒犯」（英式拼写）
由表示「反」的 counter- 与 offensive 复合而成，义为「反攻」

senses.title: Causing someone to feel insulted
senses.definition: causing someone to feel hurt, angry or insulted
senses.definitionCN: 使别人感到受伤、恼火或受辱的
senses.example: His remarks about her accent were offensive.
senses.exampleCN: 他关于她口音的那些话很冒犯人。
senses.why: The suffix -ive turns the act of striking against into a quality, so words and acts that wound people are called offensive.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 把「撞上去」这个动作变成一种性质，于是会伤人的话和行为就被称作冒犯的。

senses.title: Extremely unpleasant to the senses
senses.definition: very unpleasant, especially to see, smell or hear
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在视觉、嗅觉或听觉上非常令人不适的
senses.example: The smell from the drains was offensive.
senses.exampleCN: 下水道里传来的气味很难闻。
senses.why: The blow can land on the senses as well as on feelings, so the adjective also grades what makes the eyes, nose or ears recoil.
senses.whyCN: 这一击不只落在感情上，也落在感官上，所以这个形容词也能形容让眼睛、鼻子或耳朵想要后退的东西。

senses.title: Used for attack; attacking
senses.definition: designed or used for attacking, especially in war or sport
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在战争或体育中为进攻而设计或使用的
senses.example: The soldiers were trained to use offensive weapons.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们受过使用攻击性武器的训练。
senses.why: Because offendere pictured a blow aimed forward, the adjective also names whatever is built to push into the enemy's ground.
senses.whyCN: 因为 offendere 的意象是朝前打出的一击，这个形容词也就用来指一切为推进到对方阵地而准备的东西。

senses.title: A planned military attack
senses.definition: a large organized military attack, or a spell of attacking in a game
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的大规模军事进攻，或比赛中一段持续进攻
senses.example: The spring offensive opened along the whole front.
senses.exampleCN: 春季攻势在整条战线上展开。
senses.why: When the adjective names the attacking mode, it can stand as a noun for the attack itself, so the quality becomes the campaign.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词用来指进攻的方式，它就能独立成名词指进攻本身，性质于是变成了一场战役。

intro.en: Offensive is an adjective built on a Latin participle stem, and it split in English into the insulting, the disgusting and the attacking.
intro.cn: offensive 是建立在拉丁语过去分词词干上的形容词，在英语里分出「冒犯」「令人反感」与「进攻」三路。

items.en: The verb offendere meant to strike against, and its participle stem offens- carried the idea of something that has hit a target.
items.cn: 动词 offendere 意为撞上，其过去分词词干 offens- 带着「已经击中目标」的意思。

items.en: Medieval Latin offensivus, commonly derived from that stem, meant hurtful or ready to strike.
items.cn: 一般认为中世纪拉丁语 offensivus 由这个词干构成，意为会伤人的、动辄要打的。

items.en: Old French offensif took the adjective into French and passed it on to English with the sense of hurtful and attacking.
items.cn: 古法语 offensif 把这个形容词接了过去，再传入英语，带着「会伤人」与「用于进攻」两层意思。

items.en: In English the adjective grew two branches, one for insulting words and one for weapons, and the noun later named a military push.
items.cn: 在英语里这个形容词长出两支，一支指无礼的话，一支指武器，名词后来则用来指一次军事推进。

items.en: Modern English uses offensive for rude remarks, for disgusting smells, and for the attacking side in war and sport.
items.cn: 现代英语用 offensive 指无礼的话、恶心的气味，以及战争与体育中进攻的一方。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and verb behind this adjective; the near-meaning group gathers words for insult, disgust and attack.
note.cn: 形近组收这个形容词背后的名词与动词；近义组收表示侮辱、反感与进攻的词。

entries.definition: The noun for a crime or an insult, from the same Latin stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词干上表示罪行或冒犯的名词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the noun from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上名词的美式拼写。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to insult someone or to break a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 表示冒犯他人或违反规则的动词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in an insulting or attacking way.
entries.definitionCN: 表示以冒犯或进攻的方式的副词。

entries.definition: Rude and likely to humiliate the person addressed.
entries.definitionCN: 粗鲁并可能使对方受辱的。

entries.definition: Showing little respect for other people.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人缺少尊重的。

entries.definition: So unpleasant that it causes strong dislike.
entries.definitionCN: 极其令人厌恶的。

entries.definition: A planned attempt to defeat an enemy or an opponent.
entries.definitionCN: 为击败敌人或对手而计划发动的进攻。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin stem for striking, and it keeps the same forward push whether the target is a person, a nose or an army.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示打击的拉丁词干上，无论目标是个人、鼻子还是一支军队，它都保持同一个向前的推力。

normal.en: Offend plus -ive makes a quality: what is offensive has the habit of striking people.
normal.cn: offend 加 -ive 构成一种性质：会冒犯的东西带着「打到人」的习性。

normal.en: The same adjective serves for rude remarks and for attacking weapons, because both push forward.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词既修饰无礼的话，也修饰进攻的武器，因为两者都朝前推。

normal.en: Take the offensive turns the adjective into a noun phrase for going on the attack.
normal.cn: take the offensive 把形容词变成名词性短语，表示转为进攻。

normal.en: Offensiveness adds -ness to the adjective and names the quality itself.
normal.cn: offensiveness 在形容词后加 -ness，直接指这种性质本身。

normal.en: Offensive weapon is a legal phrase for something built or used to hurt people.
normal.cn: offensive weapon 是法律用语，指为伤人而制作或使用的物件。

abstract.en: A rude sentence and an advancing army share one direction: both are pushed outward, and both make people step back.
abstract.cn: 一句无礼的话与一支推进的军队共享一个方向：都向外推，也都让人后退。

abstract.en: Offensive smell arrives before words do; the nose is hit before anyone has spoken.
abstract.cn: 令人反感的气味先于语言到达；还没人开口，鼻子已经被击中。

abstract.en: The suffix -ive turns a blow into a tendency, a readiness to keep pushing against whatever is in front.
abstract.cn: 后缀 -ive 把一次打击变成一种倾向，一种不断朝前方顶撞的劲头。

examples.en: His remarks about her accent were offensive.
examples.cn: 他关于她口音的那些话很冒犯人。

examples.en: The smell from the drains was offensive.
examples.cn: 下水道里传来的气味很难闻。

examples.en: The spring offensive opened along the whole front.
examples.cn: 春季攻势在整条战线上展开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，芬西服」——哦，那套芬兰西服穿得怪，让人反感；offensive 就是冒犯的、进攻的。

root: 拉丁语 offendere（撞上、触犯）的过去分词词干 offens- 加 -ive 构成 offensivus，经古法语 offensif 进入英语；同一词干还生出 offence 与 offend。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the forward push of a blow; the adjective splits into insult, disgust and attack, and the noun names the attack itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一击向前的推力」；形容词分出冒犯、反感与进攻，名词则指进攻本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence and an army pushing out in the same direction.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话与一支军队朝同一个方向推出去。

branches.en: a mocking remark about someone's accent
branches.cn: 一句拿别人口音取笑的话

branches.en: a smell by the rubbish bins that stops conversation
branches.cn: 垃圾桶边的气味让人停住话头

branches.en: a weapon built only for hurting people
branches.cn: 只为伤人而制造的武器

branches.en: an attack opened in spring across a long front
branches.cn: 春天在漫长战线上发起的进攻

branches.en: one force that makes people step back, in words or in air
branches.cn: 同一种让人后退的力量，或在言语，或在空气里

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb of striking, its participle stem, and an adjectival suffix that turns the act into a lasting quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示打击的拉丁动词、它的过去分词词干，以及把动作变成持久性质的后缀共同构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

in an insulting or attacking way

items.meaningCN: 构成表示性质的抽象名词

definition_zh: 提供；给予；主动提出；出价；提议；报价；特价
definition_en: to give or present something to someone; to say you are willing to do something; to name a price; as a noun, a proposal, a bid or a special deal
core_image: 双手把东西捧到别人面前，等对方伸手接下
scene: 公交车上人挨着人，一位老人扶着扶手晃了一下，靠窗的年轻人抬手指了指自己旁边的空位。She offered her seat to the old man and he took it with a nod.
sceneCN: 这里 offer 是「提供、让出」（第 1 个义项：把东西给予别人）；句意是她把座位让给了老人，老人点头接受。画面里有拥挤的车厢和一个靠窗的空位。

pos.zh: 提供；给予；主动提出；出价
提议；报价；录用通知；特价

derivatives.zh: 由 offer 加 -ing 构成，义为「献上的东西；祭品；提供的服务或课程」
法律用语，由 offer 加表示「人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「提出要约的一方」
源自拉丁 offertorium，与 offer 同一词根，义为「礼拜中的奉献环节或奉献金」

senses.title: To give or present something to someone
senses.definition: to give something to someone, especially in a polite or formal way
senses.definitionCN: 尤指以礼貌或正式的方式把某物给予别人
senses.example: She offered him a cup of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她给他端来一杯茶。
senses.why: Latin offerre meant to bring something before a person, and that picture of presenting an object still drives the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 offerre 意为把东西带到某人面前，这幅「捧到人前」的画面一直支撑着第一个义项。

senses.title: To say that you are willing to do something
senses.definition: to express willingness to do something for someone
senses.definitionCN: 向别人表示自己愿意做某事
senses.example: He offered to drive us to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他主动提出开车送我们去车站。
senses.why: Once the thing brought forward can be an action rather than an object, the verb comes to mean putting yourself forward as willing.
senses.whyCN: 当被捧到人前的不再是物件而是一个行动，这个动词就引申为「把自己递上去」，表示愿意效劳。

senses.title: To name a price for something
senses.definition: to say what price you will pay for something or charge for it
senses.definitionCN: 说出你愿意为某物支付、或为某物开出的价钱
senses.example: They offered two million for the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们出价两百万买那栋房子。
senses.why: In a market the thing brought forward is a sum of money, so presenting turns into bidding.
senses.whyCN: 在市场里，被捧到人前的变成一笔钱，于是「呈上」就转成了「出价」。

senses.title: A proposal or a job offer
senses.definition: a formal proposal, especially one made to be accepted or refused
senses.definitionCN: 正式的提议，尤指摆出来等对方接受或拒绝的那种
senses.example: The company made her an offer she could not refuse.
senses.exampleCN: 公司给了她一个无法拒绝的录用条件。
senses.why: The noun keeps the object that was brought forward, so an offer is the proposal itself, waiting for a yes or a no.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了那个被捧出来的东西，所以 an offer 就是摆在面前、等人点头或摇头的提议。

senses.title: A special price or deal
senses.definition: a reduced price or a deal advertised to attract buyers
senses.definitionCN: 为吸引买家而宣传的降价价格或优惠方案
senses.example: The shop has a special offer on coffee this week.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店本周咖啡有特价。
senses.why: When a price is put in front of a buyer as a bargain, the same noun narrows to the attractive deal on the label.
senses.whyCN: 当价格作为便宜货摆到买家面前，同一个名词就收窄为标签上那个吸引人的优惠。

intro.en: Offer goes back to a Latin verb meaning to bring before, was borrowed early into Old English for sacrifice, and was then widened by French to any kind of presenting.
intro.cn: offer 可追到拉丁语中意为「带到面前」的动词，早期借入古英语时指献祭，后经法语扩展为一切形式的呈上。

items.en: Offerre joined ob-, meaning toward or before, with ferre, meaning to bring, so it meant to bring something before someone.
items.cn: offerre 把表示「向前、对着」的 ob- 与表示「带来、搬运」的 ferre 合在一起，意为把东西带到某人面前。

items.en: Old English borrowed the Latin verb early as offrian, and its first use was bringing a sacrifice before God.
items.cn: 古英语早期就把这个拉丁动词借进来写作 offrian，最初用于把祭品献到神面前。

items.en: Norman French offrir reinforced the word and widened it from sacrifice to any act of presenting.
items.cn: 诺曼法语 offrir 重新加固了这个词，并把「献祭」扩展为任何形式的呈上。

items.en: Middle English offer covered presenting gifts, making a proposal and naming a price.
items.cn: 中古英语的 offer 已覆盖呈上礼物、提出建议与开出价钱。

items.en: Modern English keeps the religious echo in offering and offertory, and the commercial sense in bid and special offer.
items.cn: 现代英语在 offering 与 offertory 里保留宗教余音，在出价与特价里保留商业含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derivatives and other words built on the Latin verb for carrying; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for giving, proposing and bidding.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及同样建立在拉丁语「搬运」动词上的词；近义组收表示给予、提议与出价的动词。

entries.definition: Something presented, especially to a god or to a fund.
entries.definitionCN: 献上的东西，尤指献神或捐献之物。

entries.definition: The part of a church service when gifts are collected.
entries.definitionCN: 礼拜中收集奉献的环节。

entries.definition: To send a matter or a person to another source, built on the Latin verb for carrying.
entries.definitionCN: 把事务或人转到另一处，建立在拉丁语「搬运」动词上。

entries.definition: To move something from one place to another, with the same carrying root.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从一处移到另一处，共享同一个「搬运」词根。

entries.definition: To give or hand something to someone, often formally.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物给予或递交某人，常用于正式场合。

entries.definition: To suggest a plan or an idea for others to consider.
entries.definitionCN: 提出计划或想法供他人考虑。

entries.definition: An offer of a particular amount of money for something.
entries.definitionCN: 为某物开出的某个数目的价钱。

entries.definition: To give someone something they need.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人提供其需要的东西。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb for bringing something forward, and its family keeps the picture of a gift placed in front of another person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语「把东西向前带」的动词上，同族词始终保留「把礼物摆到别人面前」的画面。

normal.en: Offerre is ob- plus ferre, so the word pictures someone bringing an object forward into view.
normal.cn: offerre 是 ob- 加 ferre，画面就是有人把东西向前带到别人眼前。

normal.en: Old English offrian first meant to sacrifice, which is why offering still sounds religious.
normal.cn: 古英语 offrian 最初指献祭，所以 offering 至今还带宗教味道。

normal.en: Offering adds -ing to offer and names the thing that was placed before someone.
normal.cn: offering 在 offer 后加 -ing，指那个被摆到人前的东西。

normal.en: Offer to do takes an infinitive and marks willingness rather than an object.
normal.cn: offer to do 后面接不定式，标出的是意愿，而不是一件物件。

normal.en: On offer is the British phrase for goods that are available or reduced in price.
normal.cn: on offer 是英式说法，指商品可买到或正在减价。

abstract.en: Picture both hands holding something out at arm's length, waiting for the other person to reach back.
abstract.cn: 想象双手把东西捧出一臂远，等着对方也伸出手来。

abstract.en: A bid is money pushed onto the table, and the other side still has to nod.
abstract.cn: 出价就是把钱推到桌面上，另一头还得点头才行。

abstract.en: Offering help means extending a hand before anyone asks for it.
abstract.cn: 主动帮忙，就是在别人开口之前先把手伸出去。

examples.en: She offered her seat to the old man.
examples.cn: 她把座位让给了那位老人。

examples.en: He offered to drive us to the station.
examples.cn: 他主动提出开车送我们去车站。

examples.en: The company made her an offer she could not refuse.
examples.cn: 公司给了她一个无法拒绝的录用条件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，发了」——哦，发了笔财，是因为有人给你出了个好价；offer 就是提供与出价。

root: 拉丁语 offerre（带到面前）由 ob-（向前、对着）加 ferre（带来、搬运）构成，古英语早期借入作 offrian 表示献祭，又经古法语 offrir 加固；同族词有 offering、offertory。

sensesIntro.en: The core is bringing something before a person; the senses divide into giving, volunteering, naming a price, a proposal and a bargain.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西带到人面前」；义项分为给予、主动提出、出价、提议与优惠。

core.cn: 核心意象：双手把一件东西捧向另一个人。

branches.cn: 一杯茶被轻轻推到桌子对面

branches.cn: 一个人说愿意开车送大家回家

definition_en: a room or building where people do their desk work; also a position of authority, a branch of an organization or government, and the duty attached to a post

scene: 清晨楼道里还没开灯，靠窗那张写字台已经摊开文件，印章和文件夹摆得整整齐齐。The office stayed quiet until the first cup of tea was finished.
